definition_en: a person trained in the science of nutrition who advises people on what to eat for health
core_image: 一个人站在餐盘旁，把食物按营养素分类、称量，并写下饮食建议
scene: The nutritionist put the patient on a diet rich in iron and fibre.
sceneCN: 这里 nutritionist 指「临床营养师」（第 2 个义项：在医院里为病人设计治疗饮食的专业人员）；句意：营养师给这位病人安排了富含铁和膳食纤维的饮食。图中可辨识物件：餐盘、食物模型、营养成分表、病历夹。

pos.zh: 营养学家；营养师（受过营养学训练、为个人或群体提供饮食建议的人）

senses.title: Nutrition scientist
senses.titleCN: 营养学家：研究营养素如何作用于人体
senses.definition: a scientist who studies how nutrients affect growth, health and disease
senses.definitionCN: 研究营养素如何影响生长、健康与疾病的科学家
senses.example: The nutritionist measured the children's iron intake over a month.
senses.exampleCN: 这位营养学家测量了孩子们一个月的铁摄入量。
senses.why: Latin nutrire 'to nourish' plus -ist 'one who practises' first named a specialist in the young science of nutrition; the laboratory sense is the oldest one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」加 -ist「从事者」，最初指新兴营养科学中的专业人员；实验室研究义是最早的义项。

senses.title: Clinical dietitian
senses.titleCN: 临床营养师：为病人设计治疗饮食
senses.definition: a specialist, usually in a hospital, who plans meals and tube feeding for patients with medical conditions
senses.definitionCN: 通常在医院工作，为患病者安排饮食与管饲方案的专业人员
senses.example: The nutritionist put the patient on a diet rich in iron and fibre.
senses.exampleCN: 营养师给这位病人安排了富含铁和膳食纤维的饮食。
senses.why: Hospitals needed a staff member to turn a diagnosis into a menu, so the word moved from the laboratory to the ward.
senses.whyCN: 医院需要有人把诊断变成菜单，于是这个词从实验室走进了病房。

senses.title: Sports nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 运动营养师：为训练与比赛配餐
senses.definition: a practitioner who adjusts energy, protein and fluid intake for athletes and training cycles
senses.definitionCN: 为运动员和训练周期调整能量、蛋白质与液体摄入的从业者
senses.example: The team hired a nutritionist to plan meals before the marathon.
senses.exampleCN: 球队聘请了一位营养师来规划马拉松前的饮食。
senses.why: Sport created a market for timed eating: nutrients are treated as fuel for a scheduled performance.
senses.whyCN: 竞技体育催生了「按时吃饭」的市场：营养素被当作按赛程供应的燃料。

senses.title: Public health nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 公共营养师：面向人群而非个人
senses.definition: a professional who designs programmes and policies about diet for whole communities
senses.definitionCN: 为整个社区设计饮食方案与政策的专业人员
senses.example: Public health nutritionists pushed for free school breakfasts.
senses.exampleCN: 公共营养师推动学校提供免费早餐。
senses.why: The same expertise is applied to populations, so the unit of work changes from one plate to a thousand plates.
senses.whyCN: 同样的专业知识被用到人群层面，工作单位从一张餐盘变成上千张餐盘。

senses.title: Food industry adviser
senses.titleCN: 食品行业营养顾问：参与配方与标签
senses.definition: a nutrition expert employed by a food company to shape recipes, claims and labels
senses.definitionCN: 受雇于食品企业，参与配方、营养声称与标签制定的营养专家
senses.example: The company's nutritionist rewrote the label to meet the new sugar rules.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的营养顾问重写了标签，以满足新的糖含量规定。
senses.why: Regulation turned nutritional knowledge into a commercial and legal service, a sense the word acquired in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 法规把营养知识变成商业与法律服务，这是该词在 20 世纪获得的义项。

senses.title: Researcher and writer
senses.titleCN: 营养研究者与科普作者
senses.definition: a person who studies diets and publishes findings or advice for the general reader
senses.definitionCN: 研究饮食并面向普通读者发表研究结果或建议的人
senses.example: The nutritionist wrote a column debunking detox diets.
senses.exampleCN: 这位营养学者写专栏驳斥「排毒饮食」。
senses.why: Popular publishing gave the title a public voice, distinct from both the clinic and the company.
senses.whyCN: 大众出版让这个头衔有了公共发声的角色，与诊所和企业的身份都不同。

senses.title: Private consultant
senses.titleCN: 私人营养顾问：一对一收费咨询
senses.definition: a practitioner who sells one-to-one dietary advice outside hospitals and sports clubs
senses.definitionCN: 在医院与运动队之外，以一对一方式出售饮食建议的从业者
senses.example: She sees a nutritionist privately every other week.
senses.exampleCN: 她每两周自费看一次私人营养顾问。
senses.why: The word follows the modern shift of advice into a paid service sold directly to the client.
senses.whyCN: 这个词跟随现代趋势，把建议变成直接卖给客户的付费服务。

senses.title: Animal nutritionist
senses.titleCN: 动物营养师：配饲料与养殖方案
senses.definition: an expert who formulates feed for farm animals, pets or zoo animals
senses.definitionCN: 为家畜、宠物或动物园动物配制饲料的专家
senses.example: The farm's nutritionist balanced the ration for the dairy herd.
senses.exampleCN: 农场的动物营养师为奶牛群平衡了日粮。
senses.why: Animal husbandry adopted the same science early, because feed conversion is measured in money.
senses.whyCN: 畜牧业很早就采用了同一门科学，因为饲料转化率直接以金钱计量。

senses.title: Self-styled expert
senses.titleCN: 「营养大师」：无资质却自称专家（含贬义）
senses.definition: loosely, a person who gives diet advice without formal qualification, often used with disapproval
senses.definitionCN: 泛指未经正式资质却提供饮食建议的人，常带不赞许意味
senses.example: Online nutritionists sell supplements with no evidence behind them.
senses.exampleCN: 网上的「营养大师」推销毫无证据支持的补充剂。
senses.why: Because the title is unregulated in many places, it can be claimed by anyone, and the word gained this sceptical edge.
senses.whyCN: 由于许多地方并不监管这个头衔，任何人都能自称，这个词因此带上了怀疑色彩。

intro.en: Nutritionist is Latin nutrire 'to nourish' plus the agent suffix -ist, mediated by the noun nutrition. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: nutritionist 由拉丁 nutrire「滋养」加表人后缀 -ist 构成，中间经由名词 nutrition。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin nutrire meant 'to nourish, to suckle'. The related noun nutrix 'wet nurse' shows the earliest picture: feeding is something one person does for another.
items.cn: 拉丁 nutrire 意为「滋养、哺乳」。相关名词 nutrix「乳母」显示了最早的画面：喂养是一个人替另一个人做的事。

items.en: Nutritio, nutritionis named the act of nourishing. Classical writers used it for feeding and rearing rather than for a modern science.
items.cn: nutritio、nutritionis 指滋养这一动作。古典作家用它表示喂养与抚育，而不是现代意义上的科学。

items.en: English nutrition entered in the fourteenth century through Old French, still meaning the act of nourishing or being nourished.
items.cn: 英语 nutrition 于 14 世纪经由古法语进入，仍指滋养或被滋养的动作。

items.en: In the nineteenth century chemists began measuring calories, proteins and minerals, and nutrition became a laboratory discipline with its own methods.
items.cn: 19 世纪化学家开始测量热量、蛋白质与矿物质，营养学成为一门有自身方法的实验学科。

items.en: The agent noun nutritionist is recorded in the early twentieth century, around the 1920s. The exact first citation is uncertain, and the title has never been legally protected in many countries.
items.cn: 表人名词 nutritionist 记录于 20 世纪初，约在 1920 年代。最早的确切书证年代存疑，而且这个头衔在许多国家从未受法律保护。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English date of nutritionist is not firmly fixed, and the deeper Indo-European root behind Latin nutrire is a reconstruction, not a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：nutritionist 的英语首见年代无定论；拉丁 nutrire 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words from the same Latin family or the same professional field that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the person who gives dietary advice.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或同一职业领域、容易混淆的词；第二组是「提供饮食建议的人」的近义词。

entries.definition: In many countries a legally protected title requiring registration and clinical training; nutritionist is often the unregulated word.
entries.definitionCN: 在许多国家是受法律保护、需要注册与临床训练的头衔；nutritionist 则常是不受监管的说法。

entries.definition: The science or the process of nourishing. It names the subject, while nutritionist names the practitioner.
entries.definitionCN: 指营养学或滋养过程，命名的是学科，而 nutritionist 命名的是从业者。

entries.definition: Means 'full of nutrients', and is said of food rather than of people or careers.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「有营养的」，用于形容食物，而不是人或职业。

entries.definition: Means 'concerning nutrition', as in nutritional value; it describes a property, not a person.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「营养方面的」，如 nutritional value；它描述属性，不指人。

entries.definition: A near-synonym in hospitals, but the two titles differ in law and training in many countries.
entries.definitionCN: 在医院语境里是近义词，但在许多国家两者在法律地位与训练要求上并不相同。

entries.definition: A person who mainly helps a client keep to a plan; coaching stresses habits, not clinical assessment.
entries.definitionCN: 主要帮客户坚持计划的人；coaching 强调习惯，而不是临床评估。

entries.definition: An expert in how food is processed, preserved and formulated; the focus is the product rather than the eater.
entries.definitionCN: 研究食品加工、保藏与配方的专家，关注产品而非进食者。

entries.definition: A practitioner of a alternative tradition that may include diet advice; the training and evidence base differ from nutrition science.
entries.definitionCN: 属于另一套替代医学传统的从业者，可能也提供饮食建议，但其训练与证据基础不同于营养科学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: nutri- 'nourish' + -tion 'the field' + -ist 'the person'.
normal.cn: nutri-「滋养」+ -tion「领域」+ -ist「人」。

normal.en: The family runs nutrition, nutritional, nutritious, nutrient and nourish.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nutrition、nutritional、nutritious、nutrient、nourish。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the workplace: clinical nutritionist, sports nutritionist, registered nutritionist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出工作场景：临床营养师、运动营养师、注册营养师。

normal.en: -ist names a person, -tion names a field, -ous describes food.
normal.cn: -ist 指人，-tion 指领域，-ous 形容食物。

normal.en: dietitian is the regulated title; nutritionist is the looser one.
normal.cn: dietitian 是受监管的头衔，nutritionist 则较宽松。

abstract.en: Picture a plate divided like a pie chart, each slice a nutrient group.
abstract.cn: 想象一只餐盘被分成饼图，每一块代表一类营养素。

abstract.en: Picture a small label being turned over to read the numbers on the back.
abstract.cn: 想象有人翻过一张小标签，读背面的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a prescription pad on which meals are written instead of pills.
abstract.cn: 想象一张处方笺，上面写的是饭菜而不是药片。

examples.en: A nutritionist helped the team plan meals before the marathon.
examples.cn: 一位营养师帮球队规划了马拉松前的饮食。

examples.en: The hospital's nutritionist adjusted her diet after surgery.
examples.cn: 医院的营养师在她手术后调整了饮食。

examples.en: Nutritionists disagree about how much protein older adults need.
examples.cn: 营养学家对老年人需要多少蛋白质存在分歧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nutri 滋养 + tion 学问 + ist 人」——研究怎么滋养身体的人 → nutritionist 营养师

root: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」→ nutritio「营养」→ 英语 nutrition + -ist「从事者」→ nutritionist。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: knowledge about nourishing a body leaves the laboratory and is applied to a patient, an athlete, a population, a product, a farm animal, or merely sold as advice.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：关于「如何滋养身体」的知识离开实验室，被用到一个病人、一名运动员、一群居民、一件产品、一头农场动物身上，或仅仅被当作建议出售。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a plate being measured and a set of food rules being written down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只餐盘被称量，一套饮食规则被写下来。

branches.en: LABORATORY AND WARD: the same expertise serves both the research bench and the hospital bedside.
branches.cn: 实验室与病房：同一套专业知识既服务研究台，也服务医院床边。

branches.en: PERFORMANCE AND PUBLIC HEALTH: nutrients are planned for a race or for a whole generation of schoolchildren.
branches.cn: 竞技与公共健康：营养素既为一场比赛安排，也为整整一代学童安排。

branches.en: THE MARKET: food companies hire the same knowledge to shape recipes, claims and labels.
branches.cn: 市场一端：食品企业购买同一套知识来塑造配方、声称与标签。

branches.en: VOICE AND FEE: the title also names a public writer and a private consultant paid by the hour.
branches.cn: 发声与收费：这个头衔也指公共写作者和按小时收费的私人顾问。

branches.en: BEYOND THE CLINIC: the word reaches farm animals, and it can also be claimed by people with no qualification at all.
branches.cn: 诊所之外：这个词延伸到农场动物，也可能被完全无资质的人拿来自称。

intro.en: Nutritionist is a Latin root of nourishing, a noun of action, and an agent suffix: nutri- plus -tion plus -ist.
intro.cn: nutritionist 由表示「滋养」的拉丁词根、动作名词后缀与表人后缀构成：nutri- 加 -tion 再加 -ist。

latinIntro.en: Latin nutrire 'to nourish' supplies nutrition, nutritious, nutrient, nutriment and, through Old French, the verb nourish; nutrix 'wet nurse' belongs to the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 nutrire「滋养」衍生了 nutrition、nutritious、nutrient、nutriment，并经古法语产生动词 nourish；nutrix「乳母」也属同一词族。

items.example: The nutritionist reviewed the cafeteria menu.
items.exampleCN: 营养师审阅了食堂菜单。

items.meaning: the act or science of nourishing
items.example: Nutrition is taught in the medical curriculum.
items.exampleCN: 营养学被纳入医学课程。

items.example: Beans are a cheap and nutritious food.
items.exampleCN: 豆类是一种便宜而富有营养的食物。

items.example: The label lists the nutritional value per serving.
items.exampleCN: 标签列出了每份的营养价值。

items.example: The broth provided warmth and nutriment.
items.exampleCN: 这碗汤提供了热量与营养。

items.example: Plants take up nutrients through their roots.
items.exampleCN: 植物通过根部吸收养分。

items.structure: Old French norir, from Latin nutrire
items.meaning: to feed and cause to grow
items.example: Good soil nourishes the seedlings.
items.exampleCN: 好土滋养幼苗。

items.meaning: poor nourishment caused by an inadequate diet
items.meaningCN: 饮食不足造成的营养不良
items.example: Malnutrition slows a child's growth.
items.exampleCN: 营养不良会延缓儿童生长。

latinEntries.meaning: to nourish, to suckle, to rear

definition_zh: 消化；消化过程；（对信息或经历的）消化吸收
definition_en: the process by which food is broken down into substances the body can absorb, or the mental process of absorbing information
core_image: 一块食物在消化道里被逐步拆小、溶开，最后变成可被吸收的细小分子
scene: Chewing slowly aids digestion by giving enzymes more time to act.
sceneCN: 这里 digestion 指「消化过程」（第 3 个义项：食物在消化道中被机械与化学作用分解的全过程）；句意：细嚼慢咽有助于消化，因为酶有更多时间起作用。图中可辨识物件：牙齿、食管、胃、小肠、消化酶示意。

pos.zh: 消化；消化过程；消化能力；（对信息、经历的）消化吸收（不可数，指具体一次消化时用复数 digestions）

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: digestion（指过程整体时通常不加 -s）

senses.title: Mechanical breakdown
senses.titleCN: 机械消化：咀嚼与蠕动把食物弄碎
senses.definition: the physical part of digestion, in which teeth crush food and the gut wall churns it
senses.definitionCN: 消化中的物理部分，牙齿把食物压碎、肠壁把它搅动
senses.example: Mechanical digestion begins the moment you bite into an apple.
senses.exampleCN: 你咬下苹果的那一刻，机械消化就开始了。
senses.why: Latin digerere meant 'to separate, to carry apart'; the first step of that separating is simply breaking a mass into smaller pieces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 digerere 意为「分开、搬运开来」；这种分开的第一步，就是把一整块弄成更小的块。

senses.title: Chemical breakdown
senses.titleCN: 化学消化：酸与酶把食物分解成分子
senses.definition: the chemical part of digestion, in which acid and enzymes split large molecules into absorbable ones
senses.definitionCN: 消化中的化学部分，酸与酶把大分子拆成可吸收的小分子
senses.example: Chemical digestion of protein starts in the stomach.
senses.exampleCN: 蛋白质的化学消化从胃里开始。
senses.why: Once chemists identified enzymes, the 'separating' action could be described as a chemical splitting rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 化学家识别出酶之后，「分开」这一动作便可描述为化学拆分，而非物理弄碎。

senses.title: The whole digestive process
senses.titleCN: 消化过程：从入口到吸收的整条流程
senses.definition: the complete sequence from chewing to absorption, taken as one process
senses.definitionCN: 从咀嚼到吸收的完整序列，作为一个整体过程来看
senses.example: Chewing slowly aids digestion by giving enzymes more time to act.
senses.exampleCN: 细嚼慢咽有助于消化，因为酶有更多时间起作用。
senses.why: The noun of action naturally names the whole event, not just one stage inside it.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词天然指整个事件，而不只是其中的某个阶段。

senses.title: Digestive capacity
senses.titleCN: 消化能力：一个人能处理好食物的程度
senses.definition: a person's or an animal's ability to deal with a particular food without discomfort
senses.definitionCN: 人或动物处理某种食物而不感到不适的能力
senses.example: Rich sauces are beyond my digestion.
senses.exampleCN: 油腻的酱汁我的肠胃消化不了。
senses.why: The process came to stand for the capacity to carry it out, a common shift from action to ability.
senses.whyCN: 过程转而代表完成该过程的能力，这是「动作转能力」的常见引申。

senses.title: Absorption after breakdown
senses.titleCN: 消化吸收：分解之后的养分进入体内
senses.definition: the outcome of digestion, namely nutrients passing through the gut wall into the blood
senses.definitionCN: 消化的结果，即养分穿过肠壁进入血液
senses.example: Poor digestion limits how much iron the body actually gets.
senses.exampleCN: 消化不佳会限制身体实际获得的铁量。
senses.why: In nutrition writing the word often includes the absorption that follows, because the two are measured together.
senses.whyCN: 在营养学写作中，这个词常把随后的吸收也算进来，因为两者是一起测量的。

senses.title: Anaerobic digestion
senses.titleCN: 厌氧消化：微生物在无氧条件下分解有机物
senses.definition: in waste treatment, the breakdown of organic matter by microorganisms without oxygen, producing biogas
senses.definitionCN: 在废物处理中，微生物在无氧条件下分解有机物并产生沼气
senses.example: The plant turns food waste into gas through anaerobic digestion.
senses.exampleCN: 该厂通过厌氧消化把厨余变成燃气。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the bodily word for an industrial version of the same breaking-down of organic matter.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用了身体里的词，指工业上对有机物进行的同类分解。

senses.title: Mental assimilation
senses.titleCN: 信息消化：把读到的内容变成自己的理解
senses.definition: the process of understanding and absorbing ideas, news or a book over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移理解并吸收观点、消息或一本书的过程
senses.example: The report needs a week of digestion before we act on it.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告需要我们消化一周，再据此行动。
senses.why: The metaphor is old: ideas are food that must be broken down before they can nourish thought.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻很古老：观点是食物，必须先被分解，才能滋养思想。

senses.title: Digestion time
senses.titleCN: 消化时间：食物在体内停留多久
senses.definition: the period a meal takes to move through the stomach and gut
senses.definitionCN: 一餐食物通过胃与肠道所需的时间
senses.example: Fat slows digestion, which is why a heavy lunch keeps you full.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪会延长消化时间，所以一顿油腻的午餐让人久饱。
senses.why: Time is the measurable face of the process, so the noun often stands for its duration.
senses.whyCN: 时间是这一过程可测量的一面，因此这个名词常直接表示其时长。

senses.title: Settling an experience
senses.titleCN: 慢慢消化：让经历或情绪沉淀下来
senses.definition: figuratively, the slow working-through of an event or feeling before it can be accepted
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指慢慢消化一件事或一种情绪，直到能够接受
senses.example: She needs time for the digestion of the bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 她需要时间消化这个坏消息。
senses.why: The bodily image extends to emotion: what is hard to take in must first be broken down internally.
senses.whyCN: 身体的意象延伸到情绪：难以接受的事，必须先在心里被拆解。

intro.en: Digestion comes from Latin digestio, built on digerere 'to carry apart, to distribute'. Its oldest sense was not about the stomach at all. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: digestion 出自拉丁 digestio，由 digerere「分开搬运、分配」构成。它最早的义项与胃并无关系。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Digerere combined dis- 'apart' with gerere 'to carry, to conduct'. It meant to separate things and carry them to their places, as an army or a household is arranged.
items.cn: digerere 由 dis-「分开」与 gerere「搬运、进行」合成，意为把事物分开并各归其位，如同安排一支军队或一个家庭。

items.en: Digestio named an arranging or distribution. Classical Latin could speak of the digestio of a meal in the sense of its being distributed through the body, not of its being dissolved in the stomach.
items.cn: digestio 指安排或分配。古典拉丁可说一顿饭的 digestio，意思是它被分配输送到全身，而不是在胃里被溶解。

items.en: Medical writers narrowed the word to the processing of food inside the body, and the older sense of orderly distribution faded.
items.cn: 医学作者把词义收窄为食物在体内的加工过程，原先「有序分配」的旧义逐渐消失。

items.en: English digestion is recorded in the fourteenth century, through Old French, already with the bodily sense alongside the general one of arranging.
items.cn: 英语 digestion 于 14 世纪经由古法语出现，已带有身体义，同时保留「安排」的一般义。

items.en: Chemistry and engineering later added chemical digestion and anaerobic digestion; the mental sense, though old as a metaphor, became common in modern writing about information.
items.cn: 化学与工程后来加入化学消化与厌氧消化；心理义虽是古老比喻，却在现代关于信息的写作中变得常见。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the semantic path from 'distribution' to 'food processing' is inferred rather than documented step by step.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与语义路径）：英语最早书证年代存疑；从「分配」到「食物加工」的语义路径属推断，并无逐步记录。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for breaking food or ideas down.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「把食物或观点拆解」的近义词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to break food down or to absorb information; as a noun it means a summary, a different line from Latin digesta.
entries.definitionCN: 动词指分解食物或吸收信息；作名词则指摘要，这条线出自拉丁 digesta，与动词义不同。

entries.definition: Means 'relating to digestion', and describes organs, juices or biscuits rather than the process itself.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「消化的」，形容器官、消化液或消化饼干，而不是过程本身。

entries.definition: Means 'able to be digested', a property of food; it does not name the process.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可消化的」，是食物的属性，不指过程。

entries.definition: Pain or discomfort from food that is not being digested well; the in- prefix reverses the healthy process.
entries.definitionCN: 食物消化不顺带来的疼痛或不适；in- 前缀把健康的消化过程反转过来。

entries.definition: The body's use of absorbed nutrients; it follows digestion rather than replacing it.
entries.definitionCN: 身体对已吸收养分的利用，发生在消化之后，并不取代消化。

entries.definition: The passage of nutrients through the gut wall into blood; digestion breaks food down, absorption moves it in.
entries.definitionCN: 养分穿过肠壁进入血液的过程；digestion 负责拆解，absorption 负责送入。

entries.definition: All the chemical reactions that use and store nutrients; it begins where digestion ends.
entries.definitionCN: 利用与储存养分的全部化学反应，起点正是消化的终点。

entries.definition: A general word for something splitting into parts; it can describe machines or arguments as well as food.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指某物分裂成部分，既可指食物，也可指机器或论证。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + gerere 'carry': food is carried apart into pieces.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」：食物被分开、被搬运成小块。

normal.en: The family runs digest, digestive, digestible, indigestion and digestibility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 digest、digestive、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: aid digestion, slow digestion, anaerobic digestion, digestion time.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：帮助消化、消化缓慢、厌氧消化、消化时间。

normal.en: Physiology separates mechanical digestion from chemical digestion.
normal.cn: 生理学把机械消化与化学消化分开。

normal.en: digestion breaks food down; absorption moves it in; metabolism uses it.
normal.cn: digestion 拆解食物，absorption 送进体内，metabolism 加以利用。

abstract.en: Picture a long river in which a lump of food is worn smaller and smaller until it dissolves.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长河，一块食物在其中被磨得越来越小，直至溶解。

abstract.en: Picture a book being cut into chapters, then notes, then ideas you can keep.
abstract.cn: 想象一本书被裁成章节，再变成笔记，最后变成你能留住的观点。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed tank where bacteria eat waste in the dark and release gas.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密闭罐，细菌在黑暗中吃掉废物并放出气体。

examples.en: Digestion of starch begins in the mouth, where saliva contains amylase.
examples.cn: 淀粉的消化从口腔开始，因为唾液中含有淀粉酶。

examples.en: A high-fibre meal slows digestion and steadies blood sugar.
examples.cn: 高纤维的一餐会减慢消化，并使血糖更平稳。

examples.en: The committee's digestion of the proposal took three meetings.
examples.cn: 委员会消化这份提案用了三次会议。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di 分开 + gest 搬运 + ion 过程」——把食物分开搬进身体 → digestion 消化

root: 拉丁 dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」→ digerere「分开搬走、分配」→ digestio「分配；消化」→ 英语 digestion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: a mass is separated into smaller parts, and that separating can be physical, chemical, industrial, or purely mental.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：一整块被分开成更小的部分，而这种分开可以是物理的、化学的、工业的，也可以纯粹是心智上的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a lump of food being carried apart into pieces small enough to pass through a wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块食物被分开搬走，直到小得能穿过一道壁。

branches.en: TWO HANDS OF THE SAME JOB: teeth and gut wall do the mechanical half, acid and enzymes do the chemical half.
branches.cn: 同一件活的两只手：牙齿与肠壁完成机械的一半，酸与酶完成化学的一半。

branches.en: THE WHOLE ARC AND ITS CLOCK: the process can be named as a single sequence, and also as the time that sequence takes.
branches.cn: 整条弧线与它的时钟：这个过程既可被命名为一个完整序列，也可被命名为它所耗费的时间。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND RESULT: the act becomes an ability, and the ability is judged by how much nutrient actually gets through.
branches.cn: 能力与结果：动作变成能力，而能力由实际有多少养分进入体内来评判。

branches.en: THE INDUSTRIAL COPY: bacteria in a tank perform the same breakdown without oxygen and produce fuel.
branches.cn: 工业复制：罐中的细菌在无氧条件下完成同样的分解，并产出燃料。

branches.en: THE MIND'S STOMACH: reports and bad news must also be broken down before they can be accepted.
branches.cn: 心智的胃：报告与坏消息同样要先被拆解，才能被接受。

intro.en: Digestion is a Latin verb of carrying apart plus a noun of action: dis- + gerere + -tio.
intro.cn: digestion 是拉丁「分开搬运」动词加动作名词后缀：dis- + gerere + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin digerere 'to carry apart' yields digestio, digestus and the English verb digest; the noun digest 'summary' comes instead from digesta, 'things arranged'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」衍生出 digestio、digestus 与英语动词 digest；名词 digest「摘要」则出自 digesta「被整理的事物」。

items.meaning: a carrying apart; the processing of food
items.meaningCN: 分开搬运；食物的加工过程
items.example: Digestion takes several hours for a fatty meal.
items.exampleCN: 一顿高脂餐的消化需要几个小时。

items.meaning: to break down food; to take in ideas
items.example: Some people cannot digest lactose.
items.exampleCN: 有些人无法消化乳糖。

items.example: The digestive tract runs from mouth to anus.
items.exampleCN: 消化道从口腔延伸到肛门。

items.example: Cooked starch is more digestible than raw starch.
items.exampleCN: 熟淀粉比生淀粉更易消化。

items.example: Cellulose is indigestible for humans.
items.exampleCN: 纤维素对人体来说无法消化。

items.example: He took an antacid for indigestion.
items.exampleCN: 他吃了抗酸药缓解消化不良。

items.meaning: the degree to which food can be digested
items.example: Cooking raises the digestibility of protein.
items.exampleCN: 烹调会提高蛋白质的可消化性。

items.meaning: a drink taken after a meal to aid digestion
items.example: They served a herbal digestif after dinner.
items.exampleCN: 晚餐后他们上了一杯草本餐后酒。

latinEntries.meaning: to separate, to carry apart, to distribute
a distribution; the processing of food

definition_zh: 消化的；助消化的；（英式）消化饼干；助消化药
definition_en: relating to the process of digesting food, or helping that process
core_image: 一条从口到肛门的管道，沿途有胃、小肠等器官在分解食物
scene: The doctor asked about his digestive symptoms after the meal.
sceneCN: 这里 digestive 指「消化系统的」（第 3 个义项：与消化道及其功能相关）；句意：医生询问他饭后出现的消化道症状。图中可辨识物件：人体消化道示意图、胃、小肠、病历问诊表。

pos.zh: 消化的；助消化的；消化系统的

forms.label: 比较级
forms.form: more digestive（较少用，多改用更具体的说法）

senses.title: Relating to digestion
senses.titleCN: 消化的：与消化过程有关
senses.definition: connected with the process by which food is broken down in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与食物在体内被分解的过程有关的
senses.example: Digestive processes begin before you swallow.
senses.exampleCN: 消化过程在你吞咽之前就开始了。
senses.why: Latin digestivus meant 'tending to break down', so the adjective starts as a description of the action itself.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 digestivus 意为「有分解倾向的」，因此这个形容词起初描述的就是动作本身。

senses.title: Helping digestion
senses.titleCN: 助消化的：帮助食物分解
senses.definition: describes a substance or drink that is thought to help the stomach work
senses.definitionCN: 形容被认为有助于胃部工作的物质或饮品
senses.example: A digestive herbal tea is sold after heavy meals.
senses.exampleCN: 大餐之后会售卖助消化的草本茶。
senses.why: The suffix -ive often marks a function, so the adjective came to mean 'serving digestion' as well as 'of digestion'.
senses.whyCN: -ive 后缀常标示功能，因此这个形容词除了「消化的」，也发展出「有助于消化的」义。

senses.title: Of the digestive system
senses.titleCN: 消化系统的：属于消化道及器官
senses.definition: belonging to the organs and tube that carry food through the body
senses.definitionCN: 属于把食物输送过身体的器官与管道
senses.example: The doctor asked about his digestive symptoms after the meal.
senses.exampleCN: 医生询问他饭后出现的消化道症状。
senses.why: Anatomy needed a compact adjective for the whole tract, and this was the readiest one.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要为整条消化道找一个简洁的形容词，这个词最顺手。

senses.title: Of digestive organs
senses.titleCN: 消化器官的：胃、肠、肝、胰等
senses.definition: describes the organs themselves, such as the stomach, intestines, liver and pancreas
senses.definitionCN: 形容胃、肠、肝、胰等器官本身
senses.example: The digestive organs receive about a quarter of the blood flow.
senses.exampleCN: 消化器官接受约四分之一的血流量。
senses.why: The same adjective shifts from the process to the body parts that carry it out.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词从过程转指执行该过程的身体部件。

senses.title: Of juices and enzymes
senses.titleCN: 消化液与消化酶的
senses.definition: describes the fluids and enzymes released into the gut to split food
senses.definitionCN: 形容释放到肠道中、用于分解食物的液体与酶
senses.example: Digestive juices are alkaline in the small intestine.
senses.exampleCN: 小肠里的消化液呈碱性。
senses.why: Once the chemistry of digestion was understood, the adjective attached naturally to the agents that do the splitting.
senses.whyCN: 消化的化学机制被理解之后，这个形容词自然附着在完成分解的介质上。

senses.title: Digestive biscuit
senses.titleCN: 消化饼干：英式名称，并非真的助消化
senses.definition: in British usage, a semi-sweet biscuit originally marketed as a digestive aid
senses.definitionCN: 英式用法，指一种半甜饼干，最初以助消化为卖点
senses.example: She had two digestives with her tea.
senses.exampleCN: 她喝茶时吃了两块消化饼干。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century bakers used the word as a health claim, and the name outlived the claim as a product label.
senses.whyCN: 19 世纪烘焙商把这个词当作健康卖点，饼干名却比这个声称活得更久，成了产品标签。

senses.title: Digestive health
senses.titleCN: 消化健康：肠道功能的整体状态
senses.definition: in health writing, the general condition of the gut, including comfort and regularity
senses.definitionCN: 在健康写作中指肠道的整体状况，包括舒适与规律
senses.example: Fibre is central to digestive health.
senses.exampleCN: 膳食纤维对消化健康至关重要。
senses.why: Modern wellness language made 'digestive' a label for a whole domain of wellbeing, not only for an organ.
senses.whyCN: 现代健康语汇把 digestive 变成一个整体健康领域的标签，而不再只指某个器官。

senses.title: A digestive remedy
senses.titleCN: 助消化药：用于缓解肠胃不适的制剂
senses.definition: as a countable noun, a preparation taken to relieve stomach trouble
senses.definitionCN: 作可数名词，指用于缓解肠胃不适的制剂
senses.example: The pharmacist recommended a digestive for bloating.
senses.exampleCN: 药剂师推荐了一种缓解腹胀的助消化药。
senses.why: English often turns an adjective into a noun for a product that embodies the quality, as with a 'sedative' or an 'aperient'.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把形容词转成名词，指体现该性质的产品，如 sedative、aperient。

intro.en: Digestive is the Latin adjective digestivus, built on digestus, the past participle of digerere 'to carry apart'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: digestive 是拉丁形容词 digestivus，由 digerere「分开搬运」的过去分词 digestus 构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Digestus, the past participle of digerere, meant 'separated, distributed, arranged'. The adjective digestivus was formed on it with -ivus 'tending to'.
items.cn: digestus 是 digerere 的过去分词，意为「被分开、被分配、被整理」。形容词 digestivus 由它加 -ivus「有……倾向」构成。

items.en: Medieval medical Latin used digestivus for things that promote or belong to the processing of food; the word stayed close to the action rather than to an organ.
items.cn: 中世纪医学拉丁用 digestivus 指促进食物加工或与之相关的事物；这个词始终贴近动作，而不是某个器官。

items.en: English digestive appears in the fourteenth century, first as an adjective of the process and soon also of the organs.
items.cn: 英语 digestive 于 14 世纪出现，最初是过程形容词，很快也用于器官。

items.en: In the nineteenth century British bakers used 'digestive' in a health claim for a mildly sweet biscuit; the name survives although the claim does not.
items.cn: 19 世纪英国烘焙商把 digestive 用作一种微甜饼干的健康卖点；声称早已不再，名称却保留下来。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation and the date when the biscuit name was coined are both uncertain; the deeper root of digerere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与饼干命名年代）：英语最早书证与饼干名称出现的年代均存疑；digerere 的更深词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family or the same spelling area; the second holds near-synonyms that name the gut and its workings.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或拼写相近的词；第二组是命名肠道及其运作的近义词。

entries.definition: The process itself; the adjective describes what belongs to that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；形容词则描述属于该过程的事物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to break food down or absorb ideas; it names the action, not a quality.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指分解食物或吸收观点；它命名动作，而非性质。

entries.definition: A property of food, meaning it can be digested; digestive describes the machinery or the process.
entries.definitionCN: 食物的属性，意为可被消化；digestive 描述机制或过程。

entries.definition: An uncommon adjective meaning 'not promoting digestion' or 'suffering poor digestion'
entries.definitionCN: 罕用形容词，意为「不利于消化的」或「消化不佳的」。

entries.definition: The technical adjective for the stomach and intestines; it is more formal and more precise than digestive.
entries.definitionCN: 指胃与肠的专业形容词，比 digestive 更正式、更精确。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the intestines, whereas digestive covers mouth to anus.
entries.definitionCN: 专指肠道，而 digestive 覆盖从口到肛门。

entries.definition: Relating only to the stomach; it is narrower than digestive.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指胃部，比 digestive 范围窄。

entries.definition: Relating to food and the tube that carries it, as in alimentary canal; it stresses nourishment rather than breakdown.
entries.definitionCN: 指食物及输送食物的管道，如消化道；它强调滋养而非分解。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: digest + -ive 'tending to': the adjective of the breaking-down action.
normal.cn: digest + -ive「有……倾向」：分解动作的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs digest, digestion, digestible, indigestion and digestibility.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 digest、digestion、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: digestive system, digestive tract, digestive enzyme, digestive health.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：消化系统、消化道、消化酶、消化健康。

normal.en: A digestive biscuit is a British product name, not a medicine.
normal.cn: digestive biscuit 是英国产品名，并不是药。

normal.en: gastrointestinal and gastric are the narrower clinical words.
normal.cn: gastrointestinal 与 gastric 是范围更窄的临床用词。

abstract.en: Picture a tube from mouth to anus, with several rooms opening off it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条从口到肛门的管道，旁边开着几个房间。

abstract.en: Picture a cup of dark tea and a round biscuit on a saucer after a heavy dinner.
abstract.cn: 想象一顿饱餐之后，茶托上放着深色茶与一块圆饼干。

abstract.en: Picture a small bottle of pills labelled for stomach discomfort in an old pharmacy.
abstract.cn: 想象旧药房里一只小药瓶，标签上写着缓解肠胃不适。

examples.en: The digestive tract is about nine metres long in an adult.
examples.cn: 成年人的消化道长约九米。

examples.en: Digestive enzymes in the small intestine finish most chemical breakdown.
examples.cn: 小肠中的消化酶完成了大部分化学分解。

examples.en: He bought a packet of digestives for the train journey.
examples.cn: 他买了一包消化饼干带上火车。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「digest 消化 + ive 的」——与消化有关的 → digestive 消化的

root: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」→ digestus「被分解的」→ 拉丁形容词 digestivus → 英语 digestive。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: the adjective of breaking food down attaches to the process, to the organs, to the juices, to a product label, and finally to a whole domain of health.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：分解食物的形容词先附着于过程，再附着于器官、消化液、产品标签，最后附着于一个完整的健康领域。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube from mouth to anus, lined with rooms where food is split.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从口到肛门的管道，沿途有几个把食物拆开的房间。

branches.en: ACTION AND AID: the adjective can describe the breakdown itself or a substance meant to help it.
branches.cn: 动作与助力：这个形容词既可描述分解本身，也可描述用来帮助分解的东西。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND ITS ROOMS: from the whole tract the word narrows to the stomach, intestines, liver and pancreas.
branches.cn: 管道与房间：从整条消化道收窄到胃、肠、肝、胰。

branches.en: THE AGENTS: juices and enzymes are the chemical hands that do the splitting.
branches.cn: 执行者：消化液与酶是完成分解的化学之手。

branches.en: THE PRODUCT SHELF: a biscuit carries the name as marketing, and a remedy carries it as a promise of relief.
branches.cn: 产品货架：饼干把这个名字当营销，药品则把它当成缓解的承诺。

branches.en: THE WHOLE DOMAIN: modern health writing uses the word for the general condition of the gut.
branches.cn: 整个领域：现代健康写作把这个词用于肠道的整体状况。

intro.en: Digestive is a Latin participle stem plus the adjective suffix -ive: digest- + -ive.
intro.cn: digestive 是拉丁分词词干加形容词后缀 -ive：digest- + -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin digerere 'to carry apart' gives digestus and digestivus; English builds digest, digestion, digestible, indigestion and digestibility on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 digerere「分开搬运」产生 digestus 与 digestivus；英语在同一词干上构造 digest、digestion、digestible、indigestion、digestibility。

items.meaningCN: 与消化有关或有助于消化的
items.example: The digestive system includes the liver and pancreas.
items.exampleCN: 消化系统包括肝与胰。

items.meaning: the process of breaking down food
items.example: Digestion begins in the mouth.
items.exampleCN: 消化从口腔开始。

items.meaning: to break food down; to absorb ideas
items.example: It takes hours to digest a heavy meal.
items.exampleCN: 消化一顿饱餐需要数小时。

items.example: Rice is easily digestible.
items.exampleCN: 米饭容易消化。

items.example: Raw cellulose is indigestible to humans.
items.exampleCN: 生纤维素人体无法消化。

items.example: Spicy food gives him indigestion.
items.exampleCN: 辛辣食物让他消化不良。

items.example: Breeders select for digestibility in forage grass.
items.exampleCN: 育种者会筛选牧草的可消化性。

items.example: The two meals differ digestively.
items.exampleCN: 这两餐在消化方面有所不同。

definition_zh: 消化；理解吸收；整理归纳；摘要；汇编
definition_en: to break food down in the body or to take in information gradually, and as a noun a summary or arranged collection of texts
core_image: 一台机器把整块原料拆开、压紧，最后输出一小叠整理好的条目
scene: The court published a digest of the new rulings.
sceneCN: 这里 digest 指「判例汇编」（第 7 个义项：把判例或法令按顺序整理成的汇编）；句意：法院出版了新判例的汇编。图中可辨识物件：厚册子、判例编号、索引标签、法院印章。

pos.zh: 消化（食物）；被消化；理解并吸收（信息）；把材料整理归纳（动词重音在后）
摘要；文摘；汇编（名词重音在前，读 /ˈdaɪdʒest/）

senses.title: Break food down
senses.titleCN: 消化食物：把食物分解成可吸收的物质
senses.definition: to break food down in the stomach and intestines so that the body can use it
senses.definitionCN: 在胃与肠道中分解食物，使身体能够利用
senses.example: Some people cannot digest lactose as adults.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人成年后无法消化乳糖。
senses.why: Latin digerere meant 'to carry apart'; the bodily sense is that carrying-apart applied to a meal.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 digerere 意为「分开搬运」；身体义就是把这种「分开搬运」用在饭菜上。

senses.title: Be digested
senses.titleCN: 被消化：食物在体内自行分解
senses.definition: of food, to undergo digestion without an expressed agent
senses.definitionCN: 指食物在体内经历消化，而不明说执行者
senses.example: Fat digests more slowly than bread.
senses.exampleCN: 脂肪比面包消化得慢。
senses.why: English verbs often alternate between transitive and intransitive, so the same form can name what the food does.
senses.whyCN: 英语动词常在及物与不及物之间交替，因此同一形式也可表示食物自身发生的变化。

senses.title: Take in information
senses.titleCN: 理解吸收：把读到的内容变成自己的理解
senses.definition: to understand and absorb ideas, facts or news over time
senses.definitionCN: 随着时间推移理解并吸收观点、事实或消息
senses.example: Give the students a minute to digest the question.
senses.exampleCN: 给学生一分钟消化这个问题。
senses.why: The food metaphor is ancient: information, like bread, must be broken down before it can nourish the mind.
senses.whyCN: 食物比喻由来已久：信息像面包一样，必须先被拆解才能滋养头脑。

senses.title: Arrange into order
senses.titleCN: 整理归纳：把散乱材料排成有条理的形式
senses.definition: to organize a mass of material into a clear, ordered form such as a table or report
senses.definitionCN: 把大量材料整理成清晰的、有条理的形式，如表格或报告
senses.example: She digested three years of records into one chart.
senses.exampleCN: 她把三年的记录整理成一张图表。
senses.why: This sense keeps the Latin idea of distribution: things are separated and put each in its place.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项保留了拉丁语「分配」的观念：把事物分开，各归其位。

senses.title: A summary
senses.titleCN: 摘要：把长文压缩成短篇要点
senses.definition: a short written summary that keeps the main points of a longer text
senses.definitionCN: 保留较长文本要点的简短书面摘要
senses.example: The journal prints a digest of each long article.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊为每篇长文刊登摘要。
senses.why: The noun comes from Latin digesta 'things arranged', a collection of excerpts set in order rather than a raw copy.
senses.whyCN: 名词出自拉丁 digesta「被整理的事物」，指按顺序编排的摘录集合，而非原样复制。

senses.title: A digest magazine
senses.titleCN: 文摘刊物：把多篇作品压缩汇编成杂志
senses.definition: a periodical that condenses articles from many sources for quick reading
senses.definitionCN: 把多个来源的文章压缩汇编、供快速阅读的期刊
senses.example: Reader's Digest made the condensed article a mass-market form.
senses.exampleCN: 《读者文摘》让压缩文章成为大众市场形式。
senses.why: The summary sense became a product category, and the noun turned into a title and a brand.
senses.whyCN: 摘要义演变为产品类别，这个名词又变成刊名与品牌。

senses.title: A legal compilation
senses.titleCN: 判例汇编：按体系排列的法令与判例
senses.definition: an ordered collection of statutes, court decisions or rules, often with summaries
senses.definitionCN: 按体系排列的法令、判决或规则汇编，通常附有摘要
senses.example: The court published a digest of the new rulings.
senses.exampleCN: 法院出版了新判例的汇编。
senses.why: Justinian's sixth-century compilation was called the Digesta, and later legal collections kept the name for arranged decisions.
senses.whyCN: 查士丁尼 6 世纪的汇编名为 Digesta，后世的法律汇编沿用此名，指按序编排的判决。

senses.title: Let something settle
senses.titleCN: 慢慢消化：让消息或经历自行沉淀
senses.definition: to allow news, an insult or an experience to sink in before reacting
senses.definitionCN: 在作出反应之前，让消息、冒犯或经历在心里沉淀
senses.example: He went for a walk to digest the bad news.
senses.exampleCN: 他出去散步，慢慢消化那个坏消息。
senses.why: The intransitive image of food settling in the body extends to feelings that need time before they are accepted.
senses.whyCN: 食物在体内安顿下来的不及物意象，延伸到需要时间才能被接受的情绪。

senses.title: Break material down
senses.titleCN: 分解物质：化学或生物处理中的降解
senses.definition: in chemistry and waste treatment, to break organic matter down by heat, chemicals or microbes
senses.definitionCN: 在化学与废物处理中，用热、化学品或微生物分解有机物
senses.example: The tank digests food waste and produces methane.
senses.exampleCN: 这个罐子分解厨余并产生甲烷。
senses.why: Engineering reuses the bodily verb for any controlled breaking-down of organic material.
senses.whyCN: 工程学把身体动词复用到任何受控的有机物分解过程。

intro.en: Digest has two Latin sources that meet in English: the verb from digerere 'to carry apart', and the noun from digesta 'things arranged'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: digest 有两个在英语中汇合的拉丁来源：动词出自 digerere「分开搬运」，名词出自 digesta「被整理的事物」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Digerere combined dis- 'apart' with gerere 'to carry'. Classical Latin used it for distributing, arranging and setting in order, not for the stomach.
items.cn: digerere 由 dis-「分开」与 gerere「搬运」构成。古典拉丁用它表示分配、安排、整理，而非胃部活动。

items.en: Digesta, the neuter plural of the participle digestus, meant 'things arranged'. It became the title of Justinian's sixth-century collection of Roman law.
items.cn: digesta 是分词 digestus 的中性复数，意为「被整理的事物」，后来成为查士丁尼 6 世纪罗马法汇编的书名。

items.en: Old French digestier carried the medical sense of processing food, and English borrowed the verb in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 digestier 带有加工食物的医学义，英语在 14 世纪借入这个动词。

items.en: The English noun digest first meant a systematic compilation, especially of law, and only later a condensed article.
items.cn: 英语名词 digest 最初指系统的汇编，尤其是法律汇编，后来才指压缩的文章。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century journalism made the condensed magazine sense common, while engineering extended the verb to industrial decomposition.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的新闻业让「压缩刊物」义流行，同时工程学把这个动词扩展到工业分解。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the first English dates of the verb and noun are approximate, and the deeper Indo-European root behind gerere is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：动词与名词的英语首见年代均为约数；gerere 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family or the same shape that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for absorbing or condensing material.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或形态相近、容易混淆的词；第二组是「吸收或压缩材料」的近义词。

entries.definition: The process itself. Digest as a noun means a summary, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程本身；digest 作名词则指摘要，不指过程。

entries.definition: Relating to digestion, as in digestive system; it cannot replace the verb.
entries.definitionCN: 与消化有关，如消化系统；它不能替代动词。

entries.definition: Means 'able to be digested'; it describes food, while digest describes the act.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「可消化的」，描述食物；digest 则描述动作。

entries.definition: A vessel or device in which organic matter is broken down, especially an anaerobic digester.
entries.definitionCN: 分解有机物的容器或装置，尤指厌氧消化罐。

entries.definition: To take in liquid, energy or knowledge; it stresses the receiving side, while digest stresses the breaking down.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收液体、能量或知识；强调接收的一面，而 digest 强调分解的一面。

entries.definition: To turn absorbed material into one's own substance, or to fit new ideas into an existing framework.
entries.definitionCN: 把吸收的物质变成自身的一部分，或把新观点纳入既有框架。

entries.definition: To state the main points of something in fewer words; it names the writing act, not the reading process.
entries.definitionCN: 用更少的词陈述要点；它命名写作动作，而非阅读过程。

entries.definition: A collection of texts or items gathered from various sources; a digest is such a collection arranged for quick use.
entries.definitionCN: 从多个来源收集文本或条目而成的集合；digest 是为快速使用而编排的这类集合。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + gerere 'carry': to carry a mass apart into pieces.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」：把一整块分开搬走。

normal.en: Noun and verb swap stress: DIGEST the summary, digEST the food.
normal.cn: 名词与动词重音互换：名词 DIGEST 是摘要，动词 digEST 是消化。

normal.en: The family runs digestion, digestive, digestible, indigestion and digester.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 digestion、digestive、digestible、indigestion、digester。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: digest food, digest information, legal digest, easy to digest.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：消化食物、消化信息、判例汇编、容易消化。

normal.en: The noun digest descends from digesta, the title of Justinian's law collection.
normal.cn: 名词 digest 出自 digesta，即查士丁尼法典汇编的书名。

abstract.en: Picture a long loaf being sliced smaller and smaller until each piece fits in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 想象一条长面包被切成越来越小的片，直到每片都能放进口袋。

abstract.en: Picture a stack of loose papers being sorted into labelled folders.
abstract.cn: 想象一摞散纸被分进贴好标签的文件夹。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed tank where waste slowly turns into gas and a dry residue.
abstract.cn: 想象一个密闭罐，废物慢慢变成气体与干燥残渣。

examples.en: Older adults often digest protein less efficiently.
examples.cn: 老年人消化蛋白质的效率往往较低。

examples.en: The weekly digest condenses twenty pages into two.
examples.cn: 这份每周文摘把二十页压缩成两页。

examples.en: It took him a day to digest the criticism.
examples.cn: 他花了一天时间消化那些批评。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「di 分开 + gest 搬」——把食物分开搬进身体，把长文分开搬成摘要 → digest 消化／摘要

root: 拉丁 dis-「分开」+ gerere「搬运」→ digerere「分开搬走、分配」；动词经古法语 digestier 入英语；名词出自拉丁 digesta「被整理的事物」。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow two linked Latin lines: the verb of carrying apart gives digestion, understanding and industrial breakdown; the noun of arranged things gives summaries, magazines and law collections.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿两条相连的拉丁线索展开：动词「分开搬运」给出消化、理解与工业分解；名词「被整理的事物」给出摘要、文摘刊物与法律汇编。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a mass carried apart into pieces, and those pieces then set in order.
core.cn: 核心意象：一整块被分开搬走，随后这些碎片被排成秩序。

branches.en: THE BODY'S WORK: the same verb covers what the stomach does to food and what food does inside the stomach.
branches.cn: 身体的工作：同一动词既指胃对食物做的事，也指食物在胃里发生的变化。

branches.en: THE MIND'S WORK: information and bad news are both taken in slowly, and both may need time to settle.
branches.cn: 心智的工作：信息与坏消息都要慢慢接收，也都可能需要时间沉淀。

branches.en: ORDER OUT OF A MESS: scattered records are separated and placed each in its position.
branches.cn: 从杂乱到秩序：散乱的记录被分开，各归其位。

branches.en: COMPRESSION: the arranged whole is shortened into a summary, and the summary becomes a magazine format.
branches.cn: 压缩：被整理的整体再被缩短为摘要，而摘要又变成一种刊物形式。

branches.en: TWO KINDS OF COLLECTION: law is gathered into an ordered digest, while organic waste is broken down in a tank.
branches.cn: 两种汇集：法律被编成有序的判例汇编，有机废物则在罐中被分解。

intro.en: Digest is a Latin verb stem with two English lives: a verb of breaking down and a noun of arranged material.
intro.cn: digest 是一个拉丁动词词干，在英语里有两条命：表示分解的动词，以及表示整理材料的名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin digerere supplies the verb digest and the nouns digestion and digesta; digestus and digestivus supply the adjectives and the industrial digester.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 digerere 提供动词 digest 与名词 digestion、digesta；digestus 与 digestivus 提供形容词及工业用 digester。

items.meaning: to break down food; a summary
items.example: The digest covers the year's key cases.
items.exampleCN: 这份汇编涵盖当年重要判例。

items.meaning: the process of breaking down food
items.example: Digestion slows during illness.
items.exampleCN: 生病时消化会变慢。

items.example: The digestive tract is long and folded.
items.exampleCN: 消化道很长且多褶皱。

items.example: Young leaves are more digestible.
items.exampleCN: 嫩叶更容易消化。

items.example: The husks are largely indigestible.
items.exampleCN: 这些外壳基本无法消化。

items.meaning: discomfort from food not digested well
items.meaningCN: 食物消化不良引起的不适
items.example: Rich food gives her indigestion.
items.exampleCN: 油腻食物让她消化不良。

items.meaning: a vessel in which material is broken down
items.example: The farm runs an anaerobic digester.
items.exampleCN: 这个农场有一套厌氧消化罐。

items.meaning: the residue left after anaerobic digestion
items.meaningCN: 厌氧消化后留下的残渣
items.example: The digestate is spread on fields as fertiliser.
items.exampleCN: 消化残渣被撒到田里作肥料。

definition_en: the process by which animals and plants remove waste substances from the body, or the waste so removed
core_image: 身体把用不上的废物筛出来，经管道排出体外
scene: The kidneys control the excretion of urea and excess salts.
sceneCN: 这里 excretion 指「肾脏排泄」（第 3 个义项：肾脏把代谢废物滤出并随尿排走）；句意：肾脏控制尿素与多余盐分的排泄。图中可辨识物件：肾脏剖面、肾单位示意、输尿管、尿液收集瓶。

pos.zh: 排泄；排泄作用；排泄物（指过程时不可数，指具体的排出物时可用复数 excretions）

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: excretion（指过程整体时通常不加 -s）

senses.title: Removal of waste
senses.titleCN: 排泄：把体内废物排出
senses.definition: the general process by which an organism gets rid of waste products of metabolism
senses.definitionCN: 生物体清除代谢废物的总体过程
senses.example: Excretion is one of the basic functions of life.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄是生命的基本功能之一。
senses.why: Latin excernere meant 'to sift out'; the noun names the separating of what the body will not keep.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 excernere 意为「筛出」；这个名词命名的是把身体不保留的东西分离出去。

senses.title: The waste itself
senses.titleCN: 排泄物：被排出的东西
senses.definition: the substance removed, such as urine, sweat or exhaled carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 被排出的物质，如尿、汗或呼出的二氧化碳
senses.example: The study measured nitrogen in the excretions of the animals.
senses.exampleCN: 研究测量了这些动物排泄物中的氮。
senses.why: The action noun can stand for its product, a common metonymy in scientific English.
senses.whyCN: 动作名词可代指其产物，这是科学英语中常见的转喻。

senses.title: Renal excretion
senses.titleCN: 肾排泄：肾脏滤出并排出废物
senses.definition: the filtering of waste from blood by the kidneys and its removal in urine
senses.definitionCN: 肾脏从血液中滤出废物并随尿排走
senses.example: The kidneys control the excretion of urea and excess salts.
senses.exampleCN: 肾脏控制尿素与多余盐分的排泄。
senses.why: Physiology assigned the general word to its main organ, since the kidney is the body's chief sifting machine.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个通用词指派给主要器官，因为肾是身体最主要的「筛子」。

senses.title: Gut elimination
senses.titleCN: 肠道排出：未被吸收的残渣离开身体
senses.definition: the removal of undigested residue through the intestines as faeces
senses.definitionCN: 未被消化的残渣经肠道以粪便形式排出
senses.example: Excretion through the gut removes fibre the body cannot use.
senses.exampleCN: 经肠道排出带走了身体无法利用的纤维。
senses.why: Although physiologists sometimes separate egestion from excretion, everyday usage places both under the same word.
senses.whyCN: 生理学有时把排遗与排泄分开，但日常用法把两者都放在同一个词下。

senses.title: Skin and lung excretion
senses.titleCN: 皮肤与肺的排泄：汗与二氧化碳
senses.definition: loss of waste through skin, lungs or gills rather than the kidney
senses.definitionCN: 废物经皮肤、肺或鳃而非肾脏排出
senses.example: Water and salts leave the body by excretion through the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 水和盐通过皮肤的排泄离开身体。
senses.why: Comparative anatomy needed the word for several routes, not just urine.
senses.whyCN: 比较解剖学需要这个词覆盖多条途径，而不只是尿。

senses.title: Drug excretion
senses.titleCN: 药物排泄：药物离开体内的速度
senses.definition: in pharmacology, the removal of a drug or its metabolites from the body
senses.definitionCN: 药理学中指药物或其代谢物离开身体
senses.example: Renal excretion determines how long a drug stays in the blood.
senses.exampleCN: 肾排泄决定一种药物在血液中停留多久。
senses.why: Pharmacology borrowed the physiological term because clearance is measured as a rate of removal.
senses.whyCN: 药理学借用了生理学术语，因为清除率正是以排出速率来衡量的。

senses.title: Excretion rate
senses.titleCN: 排泄率：单位时间内排出的量
senses.definition: the amount of a substance removed per unit of time, often per minute or per day
senses.definitionCN: 单位时间内排出的物质量，常以每分钟或每天计
senses.example: The excretion rate of calcium rises at night.
senses.exampleCN: 钙的排泄率在夜间升高。
senses.why: Clinical measurement turned the process into a quantity that can be graphed.
senses.whyCN: 临床测量把过程变成一个可以画成曲线的量。

senses.title: Plant excretion
senses.titleCN: 植物排泄：排出盐分、水分与气体
senses.definition: in botany, the removal of surplus salts, water or gases by leaves, roots or glands
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指叶片、根或腺体排出多余的盐、水或气体
senses.example: Salt excretion lets mangroves survive in salty soil.
senses.exampleCN: 泌盐作用让红树林能在盐渍土壤中生存。
senses.why: Botany extended the animal term to plants, which also sift out what they cannot store.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个动物学术语扩展到植物，因为植物同样会筛出自己无法储存的东西。

senses.title: Cellular excretion
senses.titleCN: 细胞排泄：代谢废物被运出细胞
senses.definition: the transport of metabolic waste out of a cell across its membrane
senses.definitionCN: 代谢废物跨细胞膜被运出细胞
senses.example: Cellular excretion keeps the cytoplasm from becoming toxic.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞排泄使细胞质不至于变得有毒。
senses.why: The word scales down to the cell, where the same sifting happens across a membrane.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以缩小到细胞尺度，同一种筛出于是发生在膜的两侧。

intro.en: Excretion comes from Latin excretio, built on excernere 'to sift out', from ex- 'out' and cernere 'to sift'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: excretion 出自拉丁 excretio，由 excernere「筛出」构成，而 excernere 来自 ex-「向外」与 cernere「筛」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Cernere meant 'to sift, to separate, to distinguish'. It also gives English discern and certain, because sifting is a kind of deciding.
items.cn: cernere 意为「筛、分开、辨别」。它也衍生出英语 discern 与 certain，因为筛选就是一种判定。

items.en: Excernere added ex- 'out': to sift out, to separate and remove. Classical Latin used it for bodily discharges as well as for sorting grain.
items.cn: excernere 加上 ex-「向外」：筛出、分出并清除。古典拉丁既用它指身体排出，也指筛谷。

items.en: Excretio, excretionis named the act of sifting out. The word stayed technical and uncommon in classical prose.
items.cn: excretio、excretionis 指筛出的动作。该词在古典散文中偏技术性，并不常用。

items.en: English excretion is recorded in the seventeenth century, first in medical writing about bodily waste.
items.cn: 英语 excretion 记录于 17 世纪，最早见于讨论身体废物的医学写作。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology fixed the term as the counterpart of secretion and gave it a measured rate, an organ and a cellular scale.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学把这个词固定为 secretion 的对立词，并为它配上了速率、器官与细胞尺度。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the semantic split between excretion and secretion was settled by usage rather than by any single reformer.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与语义分野）：英语最早书证年代存疑；excretion 与 secretion 的分工是用法逐渐确定的，并非某位改革者一锤定音。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused with excretion; the second holds near-synonyms for getting waste out of the body.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、易与 excretion 混淆的词；第二组是「把废物排出体外」的近义词。

entries.definition: To remove waste from the body; the verb names the act, while excretion names the process or its product.
entries.definitionCN: 把废物排出体外；动词指动作，excretion 指过程或产物。

entries.definition: Relating to excretion, as in excretory system; it describes organs, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 与排泄有关，如排泄系统；它描述器官，不指过程。

entries.definition: The waste substances themselves, always plural in form; excretion can mean either the process or the waste.
entries.definitionCN: 指排出的废物本身，形式上总为复数；excretion 既可指过程也可指废物。

entries.definition: The release of substances the body makes for a purpose, such as hormones or milk; excretion removes what is not wanted.
entries.definitionCN: 身体为某种目的制造并释放物质，如激素或乳汁；excretion 排出的则是不需要的东西。

entries.definition: A broad word for getting rid of anything; excretion is the biological case of it.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指清除任何东西；excretion 是它在生物学中的具体情形。

entries.definition: The release of a substance from a body, machine or wound; it can be normal or pathological, unlike the neutral excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 物质从身体、机器或伤口释放出来；它可以是正常或病理的，而 excretion 是中性的。

entries.definition: The technical term for removing undigested food as faeces; some textbooks keep it apart from excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 把未消化食物以粪便形式排出的专业术语；一些教材把它与排泄分开。

entries.definition: The emptying of the bowels specifically; it is narrower and more concrete than excretion.
entries.definitionCN: 专指排空肠道；比 excretion 更窄、更具体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ex- 'out' + cernere 'sift' + -tion: to sift out and remove.
normal.cn: ex-「向外」+ cernere「筛」+ -tion：筛出来并清除。

normal.en: The family runs excrete, excretory, excreta and excrement.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excrete、excretory、excreta、excrement。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the settings: renal excretion, excretion rate, drug excretion.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出场景：肾排泄、排泄率、药物排泄。

normal.en: secretion keeps what is useful; excretion removes what is not.
normal.cn: secretion 保留有用的，excretion 清除无用的。

normal.en: excreta is always plural; excretion can be uncountable.
normal.cn: excreta 总为复数；excretion 可以不可数。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve held over a bucket: small unwanted grains fall through, the rest stays.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子架在桶上：细小无用的颗粒落下去，其余留下。

abstract.en: Picture a kidney-shaped filter washing blood and sending waste down a tube.
abstract.cn: 想象一只肾形滤器冲洗血液，把废物送进管道。

abstract.en: Picture a mangrove leaf with salt crystals shining on its surface.
abstract.cn: 想象一片红树林叶子，表面闪着盐晶。

examples.en: Excretion of carbon dioxide rises during exercise.
examples.cn: 运动时二氧化碳的排出量上升。

examples.en: The drug's excretion is slowed by kidney disease.
examples.cn: 肾病会减慢这种药物的排泄。

examples.en: Marine birds excrete salt through special glands.
examples.cn: 海鸟通过特殊的腺体排出盐分。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ex 向外 + cret 筛 + ion 过程」——把废物筛出体外 → excretion 排泄

root: 拉丁 ex-「向外」+ cernere「筛」→ excernere「筛出」→ excretio「排出」→ 英语 excretion。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one movement: a body sifts out what it cannot use, and that sifting can be named as a process, as the waste, as an organ's task, as a rate, or as something a plant or a cell also does.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：身体把用不上的东西筛出去，而这次筛出可被命名为过程、被命名为废物、被命名为某个器官的职责、被命名为一个速率，也可被命名为植物或细胞同样会做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sieve that lets unwanted material pass out of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只筛子，让不需要的物质离开身体。

branches.en: PROCESS AND PRODUCT: one noun covers both the sifting and the stuff that is sifted out.
branches.cn: 过程与产物：同一个名词既指筛出动作，也指被筛出的东西。

branches.en: TWO EXITS: the kidney filters blood, while the gut carries away what was never absorbed.
branches.cn: 两条出口：肾过滤血液，肠道带走从未被吸收的部分。

branches.en: OTHER SURFACES: skin, lungs and gills also remove waste, so the word is not tied to urine.
branches.cn: 其他表面：皮肤、肺与鳃也排出废物，因此这个词并不只与尿绑定。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL NUMBER: pharmacology asks how fast a drug leaves, and physiology turns the process into a rate.
branches.cn: 临床数字：药理学问药物多快离开，生理学把过程变成一个速率。

branches.en: LIFE AT EVERY SCALE: mangroves excrete salt through leaves, and a single cell excretes waste across its membrane.
branches.cn: 各尺度的生命：红树林经叶片排盐，单个细胞则跨膜排出废物。

intro.en: Excretion is a Latin verb of sifting plus a noun of action: ex- + cernere + -tio.
intro.cn: excretion 是拉丁「筛出」动词加动作名词后缀：ex- + cernere + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin excernere 'to sift out' yields excretio and excretus, hence English excrete, excretion, excretory and excreta; excrementum gives excrement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 excernere「筛出」产生 excretio 与 excretus，因此有英语 excrete、excretion、excretory、excreta；excrementum 则给出 excrement。

items.example: Excretion keeps the internal environment stable.
items.exampleCN: 排泄使内环境保持稳定。

items.meaning: to remove waste from the body
items.example: Sea birds excrete concentrated salt.
items.exampleCN: 海鸟排出浓缩的盐。

items.example: The excretory system includes the kidneys and bladder.
items.exampleCN: 排泄系统包括肾与膀胱。

items.example: Samples of excreta were collected for analysis.
items.exampleCN: 采集了排泄物样本用于分析。

items.example: The pens are cleaned of excrement daily.
items.exampleCN: 圈舍每天清除粪便。

items.meaning: the quantity removed per unit time
items.example: The excretion rate was measured hourly.
items.exampleCN: 排泄率按小时测量。

items.meaning: removal of waste by the kidneys
items.example: Renal excretion clears most of the drug.
items.exampleCN: 肾排泄清除了大部分药物。

items.example: Excretive tissues line the salt glands.
items.exampleCN: 盐腺内衬着具排泄作用的组织。

latinEntries.meaning: to sift, to separate, to discern

definition_zh: 排泄的；排泄系统的；排泄器官的
definition_en: relating to the removal of waste substances from the body, or to the organs that do it
core_image: 一套管道与过滤器官把废物从血液和肠道里带走
scene: The excretory system removes urea, excess water and salts.
sceneCN: 这里 excretory 指「排泄系统的」（第 3 个义项：由肾、输尿管、膀胱等构成的整套系统）；句意：排泄系统清除尿素、多余的水与盐分。图中可辨识物件：双肾、输尿管、膀胱、尿道。

pos.zh: 排泄的；排泄系统的；排泄器官的
（罕用）排泄器官；排泄管（常用复数 excretories）

derivatives.zh: 执行排泄的（作定语时用）

senses.title: Relating to removal
senses.titleCN: 排泄的：与排出废物有关
senses.definition: connected with the process of removing waste substances from the body
senses.definitionCN: 与把废物排出体外的过程有关的
senses.example: Excretory processes keep the blood chemistry stable.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄过程使血液化学成分保持稳定。
senses.why: Latin -orius forms an adjective of function, so excretory begins as 'serving the sifting out'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -orius 构成功能形容词，因此 excretory 起初意为「服务于筛出的」。

senses.title: Of excretory organs
senses.titleCN: 排泄器官的：肾、鳃、盐腺等
senses.definition: describes the organs that carry out excretion, such as kidneys, gills or salt glands
senses.definitionCN: 形容执行排泄的器官，如肾、鳃或盐腺
senses.example: The kidney is the main excretory organ in mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 肾是哺乳动物主要的排泄器官。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the organ once physiology assigns the function to a specific body part.
senses.whyCN: 一旦生理学把这项功能指派给具体器官，形容词就附着在器官上。

senses.title: Of the excretory system
senses.titleCN: 排泄系统的：由器官与管道组成的整套结构
senses.definition: belonging to the whole system of organs and ducts that remove waste
senses.definitionCN: 属于由器官与管道组成的整套排废结构
senses.example: The excretory system removes urea, excess water and salts.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄系统清除尿素、多余的水与盐分。
senses.why: Anatomy needed a single adjective for the system as a unit, parallel to circulatory and digestive.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学需要为作为整体的系统找一个形容词，与 circulatory、digestive 平行。

senses.title: Of excretory ducts
senses.titleCN: 排泄管的：把废物引向体外的管道
senses.definition: describes the ducts that carry waste to the outside, such as ureters or collecting tubules
senses.definitionCN: 形容把废物引向体外的管道，如输尿管或集合小管
senses.example: An excretory duct connects each gland to the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 每条腺体都有一条排泄管通向体表。
senses.why: The functional adjective also names the plumbing that makes removal possible.
senses.whyCN: 这个功能形容词也用于命名使排出得以实现的管道。

senses.title: Of excretory products
senses.titleCN: 排泄产物的：排出的物质
senses.definition: describes the substances produced by excretion, such as urea or ammonia
senses.definitionCN: 形容因排泄而产生的物质，如尿素或氨
senses.example: Ammonia is the main excretory product of fish.
senses.exampleCN: 氨是鱼类主要的排泄产物。
senses.why: The adjective shifts from the machinery to the material result, a normal extension in scientific description.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词从机制转向物质结果，这是科学描述中的常见延伸。

senses.title: Excretory urography
senses.titleCN: 排泄性尿路造影：靠肾脏排出的造影剂显影
senses.definition: in radiology, an imaging study that follows contrast material as the kidneys excrete it
senses.definitionCN: 放射学中追踪造影剂经肾脏排出过程的成像检查
senses.example: Excretory urography showed a blockage in the left ureter.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄性尿路造影显示左侧输尿管有阻塞。
senses.why: The medical compound uses the adjective because the image depends on the organ's excretory work.
senses.whyCN: 这个医学复合词用该形容词，因为成像依赖器官的排泄功能。

senses.title: The organs as nouns
senses.titleCN: 排泄器官（名词用法，罕用）
senses.definition: rarely, the excretory organs taken as a plural noun
senses.definitionCN: 罕用，指作为复数名词的排泄器官
senses.example: The earthworm's excretories are its nephridia.
senses.exampleCN: 蚯蚓的排泄器官是肾管。
senses.why: English sometimes turns a functional adjective into a noun for the organs that embody the function.
senses.whyCN: 英语有时把功能形容词转成名词，指体现该功能的器官。

senses.title: Of excretory failure
senses.titleCN: 排泄功能衰竭的：排废能力受损
senses.definition: describes the failure or impairment of waste removal, as in excretory failure
senses.definitionCN: 形容排废功能的衰竭或受损，如排泄功能衰竭
senses.example: Excretory failure raises urea to dangerous levels.
senses.exampleCN: 排泄功能衰竭会使尿素升到危险水平。
senses.why: Clinical usage applies the adjective to the breakdown of the function, not only to healthy anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 临床用法把这个形容词用于功能的崩溃，而不只是健康的解剖结构。

intro.en: Excretory is Latin excretus, the past participle of excernere 'to sift out', plus the adjective suffix -orius. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: excretory 是拉丁 excretus（excernere「筛出」的过去分词）加形容词后缀 -orius。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Excernere combined ex- 'out' with cernere 'to sift', naming the separation and removal of what is not kept.
items.cn: excernere 由 ex-「向外」与 cernere「筛」构成，指把不保留的东西分出并清除。

items.en: The participle excretus meant 'sifted out, removed'. From it Latin built the functional adjective excretorius.
items.cn: 分词 excretus 意为「被筛出的、被清除的」。拉丁语由它构成功能形容词 excretorius。

items.en: English excretory appears in the seventeenth century in anatomical writing, mainly as a description of ducts and organs.
items.cn: 英语 excretory 于 17 世纪出现在解剖学写作中，主要形容管道与器官。

items.en: Nineteenth-century textbooks fixed 'excretory system' and 'excretory organ' as standard labels, beside the newer word 'secretory'.
items.cn: 19 世纪教科书把 excretory system 与 excretory organ 固定为标准说法，与新词 secretory 并列。

items.en: Radiology later produced compounds such as excretory urography, where the adjective marks the route the contrast material takes.
items.cn: 放射学后来产生 excretory urography 一类复合词，其中形容词标出造影剂经过的途径。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper root of cernere is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；cernere 的更深词根属重构形式，并无记录。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family or the same ending that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms that describe waste-removing anatomy.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族或词尾相同、容易混淆的词；第二组是描述排废解剖结构的近义词。

entries.definition: The process or the waste; the adjective describes what belongs to that process.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或废物；形容词描述属于该过程的事物。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to remove waste; it names the action, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，指排出废物；它命名动作，而非结构。

entries.definition: The waste substances themselves, a plural noun; excretory is an adjective and never names the waste.
entries.definitionCN: 指废物本身，是复数名词；excretory 是形容词，绝不指废物。

entries.definition: Relating to secretion, the release of useful substances; it is the near-twin of excretory and often confused with it.
entries.definitionCN: 与分泌（释放有用物质）有关；它与 excretory 形近，常被混淆。

entries.definition: Relating to urine and its organs; excretory is broader because it includes gills, skin and salt glands.
entries.definitionCN: 与尿及排尿器官有关；excretory 范围更广，还包括鳃、皮肤与盐腺。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the kidney, one excretory organ among several.
entries.definitionCN: 专指肾脏，而肾只是若干排泄器官之一。

entries.definition: A general adjective for getting rid of waste; it is not tied to a particular organ system.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指清除废物的形容词，并不绑定某个器官系统。

entries.definition: Describes glands that release useful products; the excretory glands release what the body discards.
entries.definitionCN: 形容释放有用产物的腺体；排泄腺释放的则是身体丢弃的东西。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: excrete + -ory 'serving to': the adjective of waste removal.
normal.cn: excrete + -ory「用于……」：排废功能的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs excrete, excretion, excreta, excrement and excretive.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 excrete、excretion、excreta、excrement、excretive。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: excretory system, excretory organ, excretory duct.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：排泄系统、排泄器官、排泄管。

normal.en: secretory releases useful substances; excretory removes unwanted ones.
normal.cn: secretory 释放有用物质，excretory 清除不需要的物质。

normal.en: urinary and renal are narrower than excretory.
normal.cn: urinary 与 renal 都比 excretory 范围窄。

abstract.en: Picture two bean-shaped filters with tubes running down to a bladder.
abstract.cn: 想象两只豆形滤器，管道向下通到膀胱。

abstract.en: Picture a fish's gills quietly releasing ammonia into the water.
abstract.cn: 想象鱼鳃把氨悄悄释放进水里。

abstract.en: Picture a contrast dye lighting up the urinary route on an X-ray film.
abstract.cn: 想象造影剂在 X 光片上点亮整条排尿路径。

examples.en: The excretory system includes the kidneys, ureters and bladder.
examples.cn: 排泄系统包括肾、输尿管与膀胱。

examples.en: Excretory ducts carry the gland's product to the surface.
examples.cn: 排泄管把腺体的产物送到体表。

examples.en: Excretory failure can quickly become a medical emergency.
examples.cn: 排泄功能衰竭可能很快成为医疗急症。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「excrete 排泄 + ory 的」——负责排泄的 → excretory 排泄的

root: 拉丁 ex-「向外」+ cernere「筛」→ excernere「筛出」→ excretus「被排出的」→ 拉丁 excretorius → 英语 excretory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: an adjective of sifting out attaches to the process, the organs, the ducts, the waste products and the clinical failure of the whole system.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：表示「筛出」的形容词依次附着于过程、器官、管道、排出的物质，以及整套系统的临床衰竭。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a set of filters and ducts that carry waste out of the body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一套滤器与管道，把废物带出身体。

branches.en: FUNCTION AND ITS FAILURE: the adjective describes both healthy removal and the breakdown of that removal.
branches.cn: 功能与衰竭：这个形容词既描述健康的排出，也描述排出的崩溃。

branches.en: THE ORGANS: kidneys, gills and salt glands are the parts that embody excretion.
branches.cn: 器官：肾、鳃与盐腺是体现排泄功能的部件。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS PLUMBING: from the whole set of organs down to the ducts that lead outside.
branches.cn: 系统与管道：从整套器官一直到通向体外的管道。

branches.en: THE PRODUCTS: urea, ammonia and other removed substances carry the adjective too.
branches.cn: 产物：尿素、氨及其他被排出的物质也用这个形容词。

branches.en: IMAGING AND NOUN USE: the adjective names a contrast study, and rarely stands alone for the organs.
branches.cn: 成像与名词化：这个形容词可命名一种造影检查，偶尔也独立指器官。

intro.en: Excretory is a Latin participle stem plus the functional adjective suffix -orius: excret- + -ory.
intro.cn: excretory 是拉丁分词词干加功能形容词后缀 -orius：excret- + -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin excernere 'to sift out' gives excretus and excretorius; English builds excrete, excretion, excreta, excrement and excretory on the same stem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 excernere「筛出」产生 excretus 与 excretorius；英语在同一词干上构造 excrete、excretion、excreta、excrement、excretory。

items.meaning: relating to the removal of waste
items.example: The excretory organ of an insect is the Malpighian tubule.
items.exampleCN: 昆虫的排泄器官是马氏管。

items.example: Excretion maintains the body's internal balance.
items.exampleCN: 排泄维持身体内部平衡。

items.example: The glands excrete excess salt.
items.exampleCN: 这些腺体排出多余的盐。

items.example: Excreta were sampled from the enclosures.
items.exampleCN: 从围栏中采集了排泄物样本。

items.example: Excrement attracts flies.
items.exampleCN: 粪便招引苍蝇。

items.example: Excretive cells line the gland.
items.exampleCN: 腺体内衬着具排泄能力的细胞。

items.meaning: the organs and ducts that remove waste
items.meaningCN: 负责排废的器官与管道整体
items.example: The excretory system removes urea from the blood.
items.exampleCN: 排泄系统从血液中清除尿素。

items.meaning: X-ray imaging that follows contrast as the kidneys excrete it
items.meaningCN: 追踪造影剂经肾排出的 X 线成像
items.example: Excretory urography is now largely replaced by CT.
items.exampleCN: 排泄性尿路造影现在大部分已被 CT 取代。

definition_zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；（生物的）气体交换
definition_en: the act or process of breathing, or in biology the exchange of gases between an organism and its environment and the release of energy from food
core_image: 胸腔一起一伏，空气从口鼻进入肺部，再带着二氧化碳出来
scene: Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
sceneCN: 这里 respiration 指「呼吸动作」（第 1 个义项：吸进氧气、呼出二氧化碳的生理动作）；句意：深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。图中可辨识物件：胸腔轮廓、肺、气流箭头、睡眠监测仪。

pos.zh: 呼吸；呼吸作用；一次呼吸；气体交换（指过程时不可数，指一次呼吸时可用复数 respirations）

forms.label: 不可数用法
forms.form: respiration（指过程整体时通常不加 -s）

senses.title: Breathing in and out
senses.titleCN: 呼吸动作：吸进与呼出
senses.definition: the physical act of drawing air into the lungs and letting it out again
senses.definitionCN: 把空气吸入肺再呼出的身体动作
senses.example: Respiration slows during deep sleep as the body needs less oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 深度睡眠时呼吸变慢，因为身体需要的氧气减少。
senses.why: Latin respirare meant 'to breathe again'; the noun starts as the repeated cycle of taking air and giving it back.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 respirare 意为「再次呼吸」；这个名词的起点是吸气与还气的反复循环。

senses.title: Gas exchange
senses.titleCN: 气体交换：氧气进入、二氧化碳排出
senses.definition: the exchange of oxygen and carbon dioxide between blood and air in the lungs
senses.definitionCN: 血液与肺泡空气之间氧气与二氧化碳的交换
senses.example: External respiration takes place across the alveolar membrane.
senses.exampleCN: 外呼吸发生在肺泡膜两侧。
senses.why: Physiology separated the visible movement of the chest from the chemical exchange it serves.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把可见的胸廓运动与它所服务的化学交换区分开来。

senses.title: Cellular respiration
senses.titleCN: 细胞呼吸：细胞分解有机物释放能量
senses.definition: the chemical process in cells that releases energy from glucose, usually using oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 细胞内分解葡萄糖释放能量的化学过程，通常使用氧气
senses.example: Cellular respiration turns glucose into ATP and carbon dioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 细胞呼吸把葡萄糖变成 ATP 与二氧化碳。
senses.why: The same word scales down from the lungs to the mitochondrion, because both are exchanges of gases and energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从肺缩小到线粒体，因为两者都是气体与能量的交换。

senses.title: One breath
senses.titleCN: 一次呼吸：一吸一呼的计数单位
senses.definition: a single cycle of inhalation and exhalation, used as a countable unit
senses.definitionCN: 一次吸气与呼气的完整循环，作可数单位使用
senses.example: The patient takes about twelve respirations a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 这位病人每分钟大约呼吸十二次。
senses.why: The countable sense comes from counting cycles, the way heartbeat is counted.
senses.whyCN: 可数义来自对循环的计数，计数方式与心跳相同。

senses.title: Respiratory capacity
senses.titleCN: 呼吸功能：完成气体交换的能力
senses.definition: the ability of a person or organism to carry out breathing and gas exchange
senses.definitionCN: 人或生物完成呼吸与气体交换的能力
senses.example: Illness reduced her respiration and she needed oxygen.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病削弱了她的呼吸功能，需要吸氧。
senses.why: As with many action nouns, the process can stand for the capacity to perform it.
senses.whyCN: 与许多动作名词一样，过程可以代指完成该过程的能力。

senses.title: Artificial respiration
senses.titleCN: 人工呼吸：替他人维持通气
senses.definition: the act of helping or replacing someone's breathing by machine or by mouth
senses.definitionCN: 用机器或口对口方式帮助或替代他人呼吸
senses.example: Artificial respiration kept him alive until the ambulance arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 人工呼吸让他撑到救护车到来。
senses.why: Emergency medicine turned the noun into a fixed phrase for a life-saving substitute action.
senses.whyCN: 急救医学把这个名词变成固定短语，指一种救命的替代动作。

senses.title: Plant respiration
senses.titleCN: 植物呼吸：植物同样吸氧放二氧化碳
senses.definition: in botany, the uptake of oxygen and release of carbon dioxide by plant cells, day and night
senses.definitionCN: 植物学中指植物细胞昼夜吸收氧气并释放二氧化碳
senses.example: Root respiration uses oxygen from the air spaces in soil.
senses.exampleCN: 根系呼吸使用土壤空隙中的氧气。
senses.why: Botany needed the term to correct the old belief that plants only produce oxygen.
senses.whyCN: 植物学需要这个词来纠正「植物只产氧」的旧看法。

senses.title: A living metaphor
senses.titleCN: 拟人用法：森林或城市的「呼吸」
senses.definition: figuratively, the visible rhythm of breathing attributed to a place or a large system
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，把呼吸的节律赋予一个地方或一个庞大系统
senses.example: You can feel the slow respiration of the forest at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时分，你能感到森林缓慢的呼吸。
senses.why: Writers lend the bodily rhythm to landscapes, because a forest also exchanges gases on a vast scale.
senses.whyCN: 作家把身体的节律借给风景，因为森林同样在巨大尺度上交换气体。

senses.title: Anaerobic respiration
senses.titleCN: 无氧呼吸：没有氧气也能释放能量
senses.definition: energy release from food without oxygen, producing lactate, ethanol or other products
senses.definitionCN: 无氧条件下从食物中释放能量，产生乳酸、乙醇等产物
senses.example: Anaerobic respiration in muscles produces lactate during a sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑时肌肉的无氧呼吸产生乳酸。
senses.why: The word's core is exchange and energy release, so it can name a version that needs no external air at all.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是交换与能量释放，因此也能命名一种完全不需要外界空气的版本。

intro.en: Respiration comes from Latin respiratio, built on respirare 'to breathe again', from re- 'again' and spirare 'to breathe'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiration 出自拉丁 respiratio，由 respirare「再次呼吸」构成，而 respirare 来自 re-「再次」与 spirare「呼吸」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare meant 'to breathe, to blow'. Its family is wide: spiritus 'breath, spirit', inspirare 'to breathe into', expirare 'to breathe out'.
items.cn: spirare 意为「呼吸、吹」。其词族很广：spiritus「气息、精神」、inspirare「吹入」、expirare「呼出」。

items.en: Respirare added re- 'again' or 'back': to breathe again, to recover breath, to take a rest. Classical Latin used it for catching one's breath after effort.
items.cn: respirare 加 re-「再次、返回」：再次呼吸、缓过气来、休息。古典拉丁用它指用力之后喘过气来。

items.en: Respiratio named the act of breathing again and, by extension, the ordinary process of breathing.
items.cn: respiratio 指再次呼吸的动作，并引申为一般的呼吸过程。

items.en: English respiration is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first as a general word for breathing and for rest after exertion.
items.cn: 英语 respiration 记录于 14 世纪，起初泛指呼吸以及用力后的歇息。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward physiology split the word into external respiration in the lungs and internal or cellular respiration in the tissues.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，生理学把这个词分为肺内的外呼吸与组织内的内呼吸或细胞呼吸。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper Indo-European root behind spirare is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；spirare 背后的更深印欧词根属重构形式，并非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for breathing and gas exchange.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「呼吸与气体交换」的近义词。

entries.definition: To breathe; the verb names the action, while respiration names the process or one cycle of it.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸；动词指动作，respiration 指过程或其中的一次循环。

entries.definition: Relating to breathing, as in respiratory system; it describes organs and functions rather than the act.
entries.definitionCN: 与呼吸有关，如呼吸系统；它描述器官与功能，而非动作。

entries.definition: A mask or machine that supplies air or filters it; it is a countable object, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 供气或滤气的面罩或机器；是可数物件，不是过程。

entries.definition: Sweating through the skin; it shares the Latin spirare root but names water loss, not gas exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 经皮肤出汗；它与 respiration 共享拉丁 spirare 词根，但指失水，而非气体交换。

entries.definition: The ordinary English word for moving air in and out; respiration is the technical and biological term.
entries.definitionCN: 日常英语中「吸进呼出空气」的普通词；respiration 是技术与生物学用语。

entries.definition: The mechanical movement of air into and out of the lungs; it names the transport, while respiration includes the exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 空气进出肺的机械运动；它命名输送，而 respiration 还包括交换。

entries.definition: The transfer of oxygen and carbon dioxide across a membrane; it is the functional core of respiration.
entries.definitionCN: 氧气与二氧化碳跨膜转移，是呼吸的功能核心。

entries.definition: All the chemical reactions of a living body; cellular respiration is one part of metabolism.
entries.definitionCN: 生物体全部的化学反应；细胞呼吸只是代谢的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + spirare 'breathe': breathing is a cycle that repeats.
normal.cn: re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」：呼吸是不断重复的循环。

normal.en: The family runs respire, respiratory, respirator, respirometer and respiration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 respire、respiratory、respirator、respirometer、respiration。
