normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: cellular respiration, aerobic respiration, artificial respiration, external respiration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学语境：细胞呼吸、有氧呼吸、人工呼吸、外呼吸。

normal.en: spirare also gives spirit, inspire, expire and conspire.
normal.cn: spirare 还衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire。

normal.en: Breathing is ventilation; the chemistry it enables is respiration.
normal.cn: 呼吸动作是 ventilation，它促成的化学过程才是 respiration。

abstract.en: Picture a tide going in and out of a chest, slow and even.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水在胸腔里进出，缓慢而均匀。

abstract.en: Picture a mitochondrion as a tiny furnace that takes sugar and oxygen and gives out energy.
abstract.cn: 想象线粒体是一座小炉子，吃进糖与氧，放出能量。

abstract.en: Picture a forest at dawn, mist moving as if the whole wood were breathing.
abstract.cn: 想象黎明时的森林，雾气流动，仿佛整片树林在呼吸。

examples.en: Respiration rate is one of the vital signs recorded on admission.
examples.cn: 呼吸频率是入院时记录的生命体征之一。

examples.en: Cellular respiration releases energy stored in glucose.
examples.cn: 细胞呼吸释放储存在葡萄糖中的能量。

examples.en: Anaerobic respiration allows muscles to work without enough oxygen.
examples.cn: 无氧呼吸让肌肉在氧气不足时仍能工作。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re 再次 + spir 呼吸 + ation 过程」——一遍遍再呼吸 → respiration 呼吸

root: 拉丁 re-「再次」+ spirare「呼吸」→ respirare「再次呼吸、缓气」→ respiratio「呼吸」→ 英语 respiration。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one cycle: air goes in and out, the body takes oxygen and gives back carbon dioxide, and that exchange can happen in a lung, a cell, a plant or a whole forest.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个循环展开：空气进出，身体取氧还碳，而这种交换可以发生在肺里、细胞里、植物里，也可以发生在一整片森林里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: air moving in and out of a body, taking oxygen and returning carbon dioxide.
core.cn: 核心意象：空气进出身体，取走氧气，还回二氧化碳。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE CYCLE: the chest movement and the single counted breath are the same event at two scales.
branches.cn: 可见的循环：胸廓运动与可计数的单次呼吸，是同一事件的两个尺度。

branches.en: THE CHEMISTRY: gas exchange can run with oxygen or without it, in lungs or in muscle.
branches.cn: 化学层面：气体交换可以在有氧或无氧、在肺里或肌肉里进行。

branches.en: THE CELL: the same word names the mitochondrial breakdown of glucose.
branches.cn: 细胞一端：同一个词也命名线粒体对葡萄糖的分解。

branches.en: CAPACITY AND SUBSTITUTE: the process becomes an ability, and medicine can replace it artificially.
branches.cn: 能力与替代：过程变成能力，医学也能用人工方式替代它。

branches.en: BEYOND ANIMALS: plants respire too, and writers lend the rhythm to whole landscapes.
branches.cn: 动物之外：植物也会呼吸，作家则把这个节律借给整片风景。

intro.en: Respiration is a Latin verb of breathing plus a noun of action: re- + spirare + -tio.
intro.cn: respiration 是拉丁「呼吸」动词加动作名词后缀：re- + spirare + -tio。

latinIntro.en: Latin spirare 'to breathe' supplies spirit, inspire, expire, conspire and respirare; respiratio gives English respiration, respire and respiratory.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire、conspire、respirare；respiratio 给出英语 respiration、respire、respiratory。

items.example: Respiration continues even during sleep.
items.exampleCN: 睡眠中呼吸仍在继续。

items.example: Fish respire through their gills.
items.exampleCN: 鱼通过鳃呼吸。

items.example: The respiratory tract runs from nose to lungs.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸道从鼻延伸到肺。

items.meaning: a device that supplies or filters air
items.example: The firefighter wore a respirator.
items.exampleCN: 消防员戴着呼吸面罩。

items.example: The respirometer tracked oxygen uptake in the soil.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸测量仪追踪了土壤的耗氧量。

items.example: The word spirit began as a word for breath.
items.exampleCN: spirit 最初是表示呼吸的词。

items.meaning: to breathe life into; to stimulate
items.example: The teacher inspired the class.
items.exampleCN: 这位老师激励了全班。

items.meaning: to breathe out; to come to an end
items.example: The passport expires next year.
items.exampleCN: 护照明年到期。

latinEntries.meaning: to breathe again, to recover breath
a breathing; a recovery of breath

definition_zh: 呼吸的；呼吸系统的；呼吸器官的
definition_en: relating to breathing or to the organs and passages used for breathing
core_image: 一条从鼻腔到肺泡的通路，空气沿路进出
scene: Smoking damages the respiratory tract from the throat to the alveoli.
sceneCN: 这里 respiratory 指「呼吸道的」（第 4 个义项：空气所经的鼻腔、咽、气管与支气管）；句意：吸烟损害从咽喉到肺泡的呼吸道。图中可辨识物件：鼻腔、气管、支气管树、肺泡。

pos.zh: 呼吸的；呼吸系统的；呼吸器官的

senses.title: Relating to breathing
senses.titleCN: 呼吸的：与呼吸动作有关
senses.definition: connected with the act of breathing
senses.definitionCN: 与呼吸动作有关的
senses.example: Respiratory effort increases during exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 运动时呼吸做功增加。
senses.why: Latin respiratorius is a functional adjective, so the word begins as 'serving breathing'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 respiratorius 是功能形容词，因此这个词起初意为「服务于呼吸的」。

senses.title: Of the respiratory system
senses.titleCN: 呼吸系统的：鼻腔到肺的整套结构
senses.definition: belonging to the whole system of passages and organs used in breathing
senses.definitionCN: 属于呼吸所用的整套通道与器官
senses.example: The respiratory system includes the nose, trachea and lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸系统包括鼻、气管与肺。
senses.why: Anatomy grouped the passages into one system and needed a single adjective for it.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把这些通道归为一个系统，需要单一形容词来指称。

senses.title: Of respiratory organs
senses.titleCN: 呼吸器官的：肺、鳃、气囊等
senses.definition: describes the organs that carry out gas exchange, such as lungs, gills or air sacs
senses.definitionCN: 形容执行气体交换的器官，如肺、鳃或气囊
senses.example: Bird respiratory organs include air sacs as well as lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟的呼吸器官除肺之外还包括气囊。
senses.why: The adjective attaches to the organ itself, not only to the function.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词附着于器官本身，而不只是功能。

senses.title: Of the respiratory tract
senses.titleCN: 呼吸道的：空气经过的管道
senses.definition: describes the tube from nose and mouth down to the alveoli
senses.definitionCN: 形容从口鼻向下直到肺泡的管道
senses.example: Smoking damages the respiratory tract from the throat to the alveoli.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟损害从咽喉到肺泡的呼吸道。
senses.why: Clinical writing needed a word for the route rather than for the organ at its end.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作需要指称这条路径，而非其末端的器官。

senses.title: Respiratory disease
senses.titleCN: 呼吸系统疾病：影响通气或交换的病症
senses.definition: describes illness of the airways or lungs, such as asthma or pneumonia
senses.definitionCN: 形容气道或肺部的疾病，如哮喘或肺炎
senses.example: Respiratory disease is a leading cause of hospital admission.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸系统疾病是入院的主要原因之一。
senses.why: Clinical medicine groups illnesses of the airways and lungs under one adjective because they share the same passages and the same symptoms.
senses.whyCN: 临床医学把气道与肺的疾病归在同一个形容词下，因为它们共用同一条通道，也共用同一组症状。

senses.title: Respiratory failure
senses.titleCN: 呼吸衰竭：气体交换不足以维持血液氧合
senses.definition: a condition in which the lungs cannot keep blood oxygen or carbon dioxide within safe limits
senses.definitionCN: 肺无法把血氧或二氧化碳维持在安全范围内的状态
senses.example: Respiratory failure required mechanical ventilation.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸衰竭需要使用机械通气。
senses.why: Failure names the point where gas exchange can no longer keep blood chemistry safe, so the adjective marks the breakdown of the organ itself.
senses.whyCN: 衰竭指的是气体交换已无法维持血液化学安全的那一点，因此这个形容词标记的是器官本身的崩溃。

senses.title: Respiratory rate
senses.titleCN: 呼吸频率：每分钟呼吸次数
senses.definition: the number of breaths taken per minute, a standard vital sign
senses.definitionCN: 每分钟呼吸的次数，是标准的生命体征
senses.example: The nurse recorded a respiratory rate of twenty-two.
senses.exampleCN: 护士记录呼吸频率为每分钟二十二次。
senses.why: Counting breaths per minute turns the adjective into a measurable number, the way heart rate counts beats.
senses.whyCN: 把每分钟的呼吸次数数出来，就把这个形容词变成一个可测量的数字，正如心率数的是心跳。

senses.title: Respiratory acidosis
senses.titleCN: 呼吸性酸中毒：通气不足导致二氧化碳蓄积
senses.definition: a blood chemistry disturbance caused by inadequate breathing, which retains carbon dioxide
senses.definitionCN: 因通气不足、二氧化碳滞留而引起的血液化学紊乱
senses.example: Respiratory acidosis showed up as a falling blood pH.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸性酸中毒表现为血液 pH 下降。
senses.why: Acidosis names the chemical result of retained carbon dioxide, so the adjective points to breathing as the cause rather than the effect.
senses.whyCN: 酸中毒命名的是二氧化碳滞留的化学结果，因此这个形容词指向的是作为原因的呼吸，而非结果。

intro.en: Respiratory is Latin respiratorius, formed on respiratio 'breathing', from respirare. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiratory 是拉丁 respiratorius，由 respiratio「呼吸」构成，而 respiratio 出自 respirare。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Spirare 'to breathe, to blow' underlies a large family: spiritus, inspirare, expirare, suspirare and respirare.
items.cn: spirare「呼吸、吹」是大家族的基础：spiritus、inspirare、expirare、suspirare、respirare。

items.en: Respirare meant 'to breathe again, to recover breath'. Its action noun respiratio named breathing in general.
items.cn: respirare 意为「再次呼吸、缓过气来」，其动作名词 respiratio 泛指呼吸。

items.en: Respiratorius was a functional adjective meaning 'serving breathing'. It appears in later medical Latin rather than in classical prose.
items.cn: respiratorius 是功能形容词，意为「服务于呼吸的」，见于后世医学拉丁，而非古典散文。

items.en: English respiratory enters in the seventeenth century, first in medical descriptions of the lungs and their passages.
items.cn: 英语 respiratory 于 17 世纪进入，最早见于对肺及其通道的医学描述。

items.en: Nineteenth- and twentieth-century medicine built fixed phrases such as respiratory system, respiratory tract, respiratory failure and respiratory rate.
items.cn: 19 至 20 世纪的医学构造了 respiratory system、respiratory tract、respiratory failure、respiratory rate 等固定短语。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper root behind spirare is reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；spirare 背后的更深词根属重构形式，并无记录。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the organs and functions of breathing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「呼吸器官与功能」的近义词。

entries.definition: The process or one breath; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指过程或一次呼吸；形容词描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: To breathe; it names the action, while respiratory describes a structure or function.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸；动词指动作，respiratory 则描述结构或功能。

entries.definition: A mask or machine for supplying or filtering air; a countable object.
entries.definitionCN: 供气或滤气的面罩或机器，是可数物件。

entries.definition: Relating to sweating; it shares the spirare root but concerns water loss through skin.
entries.definitionCN: 与出汗有关；共享 spirare 词根，但指经皮肤失水。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the lungs; respiratory covers nose, throat, trachea and lungs.
entries.definitionCN: 专指肺；respiratory 覆盖鼻、咽喉、气管与肺。

entries.definition: The ordinary word for the action; respiratory is the technical adjective used in medicine.
entries.definitionCN: 日常词；respiratory 是医学中使用的专业形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to the mechanical movement of air; it stresses flow rather than gas exchange.
entries.definitionCN: 与空气的机械流动有关，强调流量而非气体交换。

entries.definition: Relating to the bronchi; it is narrower than respiratory.
entries.definitionCN: 与支气管有关，比 respiratory 范围窄。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: respire + -atory 'relating to': the adjective of breathing.
normal.cn: respire + -atory「与……有关」：呼吸的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs respire, respiration, respirator, respirometer and cardiorespiratory.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 respire、respiration、respirator、respirometer、cardiorespiratory。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: respiratory system, respiratory tract, respiratory failure, respiratory rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：呼吸系统、呼吸道、呼吸衰竭、呼吸频率。

normal.en: pulmonary is only the lungs; respiratory covers the whole route.
normal.cn: pulmonary 只指肺，respiratory 覆盖整条通路。

normal.en: spirare also gives spirit, inspire and expire.
normal.cn: spirare 还衍生出 spirit、inspire、expire。

abstract.en: Picture a tree inside the chest, trunk splitting into branches and ending in tiny buds.
abstract.cn: 想象胸腔里长着一棵树，树干分叉成枝条，末端是细小的芽。

abstract.en: Picture air flowing down a corridor lined with moist pink walls.
abstract.cn: 想象空气沿着一条湿润的粉红色走廊向下流。

abstract.en: Picture a mask over a face, with a tube supplying clean air.
abstract.cn: 想象一张面罩罩住脸，管子送来洁净空气。

examples.en: Respiratory infections spread easily in crowded rooms.
examples.cn: 呼吸道感染在拥挤的房间里容易传播。

examples.en: The respiratory tract warms and moistens the air it carries.
examples.cn: 呼吸道会温暖并湿润它所输送的空气。

examples.en: Doctors watch the respiratory rate for early signs of trouble.
examples.cn: 医生监测呼吸频率以发现早期问题。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respire 呼吸 + atory 的」——与呼吸有关的 → respiratory 呼吸的

root: 拉丁 spirare「呼吸」→ respirare「再次呼吸」→ respiratio「呼吸」→ 拉丁形容词 respiratorius → 英语 respiratory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: an adjective of breathing attaches to the act, to the whole system, to the organs, to the tube, and to the diseases and measurements of that tube.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：表示呼吸的形容词依次附着于动作、整套系统、器官、管道，以及这条管道上的疾病与测量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a branching passage from nose to alveoli, carrying air in and out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条从鼻到肺泡的分叉通道，把空气送进送出。

branches.en: ACT AND ORGAN: the adjective can describe breathing itself or the lungs and gills that perform it.
branches.cn: 动作与器官：这个形容词既可描述呼吸本身，也可描述执行呼吸的肺与鳃。

branches.en: SYSTEM AND ROUTE: the whole set of organs and the tube through which air travels.
branches.cn: 系统与路径：整套器官以及空气经过的管道。

branches.en: WHEN IT GOES WRONG: disease and failure are the clinical face of the same adjective.
branches.cn: 出问题时：疾病与衰竭是同一形容词的临床面孔。

branches.en: THE MEASURED BREATH: respiratory rate turns breathing into a number on a chart.
branches.cn: 可测量的呼吸：呼吸频率把呼吸变成图表上的数字。

branches.en: THE BLOOD SIDE: respiratory acidosis names the chemical consequence of poor ventilation.
branches.cn: 血液一端：呼吸性酸中毒命名通气不良的化学后果。

intro.en: Respiratory is a Latin noun of breathing plus the functional adjective suffix -ory: respirat- + -ory.
intro.cn: respiratory 是拉丁「呼吸」名词加功能形容词后缀 -ory：respirat- + -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin respirare and respiratio give English respire, respiration, respirator and respiratory; spirare also underlies spirit, inspire and expire.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 respirare 与 respiratio 给出英语 respire、respiration、respirator、respiratory；spirare 还支撑 spirit、inspire、expire。

items.example: Respiratory muscles include the diaphragm.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸肌包括膈肌。

items.example: Respiration supplies oxygen to the blood.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸为血液供氧。

items.example: Insects respire through spiracles.
items.exampleCN: 昆虫通过气门呼吸。

items.meaning: a device for supplying or filtering air
items.example: The welder put on a respirator.
items.exampleCN: 焊工戴上了呼吸面罩。

items.example: A respirometer measured the seeds' oxygen use.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸测量仪测了种子的耗氧量。

items.meaning: relating to the heart and breathing
items.example: Cardiorespiratory fitness predicts long-term health.
items.exampleCN: 心肺适能可预测长期健康。

items.example: Spirit and respiration share a root.
items.exampleCN: spirit 与 respiration 共享词根。

items.example: The speech inspired the audience.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲激励了听众。

latinEntries.meaning: to breathe again, to recover breath

definition_zh: 呼吸频率；每分钟呼吸次数
definition_en: the number of breaths a person or animal takes in one minute, used as a basic physiological measure
core_image: 一只秒表与一起一伏的胸口，旁边记着每分钟的次数
scene: A respiration rate above twenty can be an early warning sign.
sceneCN: 这里 respiration rate 指「呼吸频率」（第 1 个义项：每分钟呼吸的次数，作为生理指标）；句意：呼吸频率超过二十次可能是早期警报信号。图中可辨识物件：秒表、起伏的胸廓、计数板、监护仪数值。

pos.zh: 呼吸频率；每分钟呼吸次数（可数，常用单数形式作指标名）

senses.title: Breaths per minute
senses.titleCN: 呼吸频率：每分钟呼吸次数
senses.definition: the count of complete breaths taken in one minute
senses.definitionCN: 一分钟内完成的完整呼吸次数
senses.example: A respiration rate above twenty can be an early warning sign.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率超过二十次可能是早期警报信号。
senses.why: Rate turns an action into a countable quantity per unit time, so breathing becomes a number.
senses.whyCN: rate 把动作变成单位时间内的可计数量，于是呼吸变成了一个数字。

senses.title: Resting rate
senses.titleCN: 静息呼吸频率：安静状态下的基线值
senses.definition: the rate measured while the subject is calm, seated and not speaking
senses.definitionCN: 受试者安静坐着、不说话时测得的数值
senses.example: Her resting respiration rate is fourteen.
senses.exampleCN: 她的静息呼吸频率是十四次。
senses.why: Baselines require a controlled state, so the phrase is qualified by 'resting'.
senses.whyCN: 基线需要受控状态，因此这个短语常用 resting 限定。

senses.title: Rate during exertion
senses.titleCN: 运动时的呼吸频率：随耗氧上升
senses.definition: the rate reached during exercise or hard work, which rises with oxygen demand
senses.definitionCN: 运动或重体力劳动时达到的频率，随需氧量上升
senses.example: His respiration rate doubled during the sprint.
senses.exampleCN: 短跑时他的呼吸频率翻了一倍。
senses.why: The measure is useful precisely because it tracks effort, so an exertional sense is standard.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标之所以有用，正因为它跟随用力程度，因此运动义是标准用法。

senses.title: Abnormal rate
senses.titleCN: 异常呼吸频率：过速或过缓
senses.definition: a rate outside the expected range, faster (tachypnea) or slower (bradypnea) than normal
senses.definitionCN: 超出预期范围的频率，比正常更快（呼吸过速）或更慢（呼吸过缓）
senses.example: A falling respiration rate worried the night nurse.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率下降让夜班护士担心。
senses.why: Clinical language needs to name deviation, so the phrase carries a diagnostic sense.
senses.whyCN: 临床语言需要命名偏离，因此这个短语带有诊断义。

senses.title: A vital sign
senses.titleCN: 生命体征：入院与查房必测的指标
senses.definition: one of the standard vital signs recorded with temperature, pulse and blood pressure
senses.definitionCN: 与体温、脉搏、血压一起记录的标准生命体征之一
senses.example: The nurse wrote the respiration rate on the observation chart.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把呼吸频率写在观察记录表上。
senses.why: Hospitals standardized four or six vital signs, and breathing was reduced to one of them.
senses.whyCN: 医院把生命体征标准化为四项或六项，呼吸被简化为其中一项。

senses.title: An animal measure
senses.titleCN: 动物生理指标：实验与养殖中的测量
senses.definition: the breathing rate of an animal, used in laboratory physiology or livestock monitoring
senses.definitionCN: 动物的呼吸频率，用于实验室生理学或养殖监测
senses.example: The calves' respiration rate rose in the hot shed.
senses.exampleCN: 犊牛在炎热的棚里呼吸频率上升。
senses.why: The measure is species-neutral, so it travels from clinics to barns and laboratories.
senses.whyCN: 这个指标不区分物种，因此从诊所走进畜舍与实验室。

senses.title: Sleep monitoring
senses.titleCN: 睡眠呼吸监测：夜间频率变化
senses.definition: the rate tracked overnight to detect pauses or drops in breathing during sleep
senses.definitionCN: 夜间持续追踪的频率，用于发现睡眠中的呼吸暂停或下降
senses.example: The sleep study logged her respiration rate every thirty seconds.
senses.exampleCN: 睡眠监测每三十秒记录一次她的呼吸频率。
senses.why: Sleep studies need a continuous record rather than one measurement, so the compound names a value tracked through the night.
senses.whyCN: 睡眠监测需要连续记录而非一次测量，因此这个复合词命名的是整夜被追踪的数值。

senses.title: Component of ventilation
senses.titleCN: 每分通气量的组成：频率乘潮气量
senses.definition: one factor in minute ventilation, which equals respiration rate multiplied by tidal volume
senses.definitionCN: 每分通气量的一个因子，通气量等于呼吸频率乘以潮气量
senses.example: Minute ventilation rises when either the respiration rate or the tidal volume increases.
senses.exampleCN: 呼吸频率或潮气量任一上升，每分通气量都会增加。
senses.why: Physiology treats the rate as one multiplier in a product, not as an isolated number.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把频率看作乘积中的一个乘数，而非孤立的数字。

senses.title: How it is counted
senses.titleCN: 计数方法：观察胸廓起伏计时一分钟
senses.definition: the practical procedure of counting chest rises for a full minute, or for fifteen seconds and multiplying
senses.definitionCN: 观察胸廓起伏满一分钟，或数十五秒再乘以四的实用方法
senses.example: Count the respiration rate while the patient thinks you are taking the pulse.
senses.exampleCN: 趁病人以为你在测脉搏时数呼吸频率。
senses.why: The phrase also names the measurement act, because a rate must be produced by counting.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语也命名测量动作，因为频率必须通过计数才能得出。

intro.en: Respiration rate joins Latin respiratio 'breathing' to rate, from Latin rata pars 'a fixed portion'. The compound is a modern physiological label. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: respiration rate 把拉丁 respiratio「呼吸」与 rate 连接起来，后者出自拉丁 rata pars「固定的份额」。这个复合词是现代生理学标签。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Respiratio, from respirare 'to breathe again', named breathing as an action.
items.cn: respiratio 出自 respirare「再次呼吸」，把呼吸命名成一个动作。

items.en: Rate descends from Latin rata pars, 'a reckoned or fixed portion', from reri 'to reckon'. Ratio and ration belong to the same family.
items.cn: rate 出自拉丁 rata pars「经计算或固定的份额」，源于 reri「计算」。ratio 与 ration 属同一词族。

items.en: English rate first meant an estimated value or a fixed charge, and only later a measured amount per unit of time.
items.cn: 英语 rate 最初指估算的价值或固定费用，后来才指单位时间内的测量量。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physiology began expressing breathing as a frequency per minute, making it comparable between patients.
items.cn: 19 世纪生理学开始把呼吸表示成每分钟的频率，使不同病人之间可以比较。

items.en: Twentieth-century hospital practice fixed respiration rate as a vital sign; 'respiratory rate' became the more common clinical wording.
items.cn: 20 世纪医院实践把 respiration rate 固定为生命体征；respiratory rate 成为更常见的临床说法。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact date when the compound was first written is uncertain, and the deeper root behind reri is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：这个复合词首次书写的年代存疑；reri 背后的更深词根属重构形式。

note.en: The first group holds closely related terms that are easily confused in clinical use; the second holds near-synonyms for the measured frequency of breathing.
note.cn: 第一组是临床使用中容易混淆的近邻术语；第二组是「测得的呼吸频率」的近义词。

entries.definition: The usual clinical wording for the same measurement; it is largely interchangeable with respiration rate.
entries.definitionCN: 同一测量在临床上的常用说法，与 respiration rate 基本可互换。

entries.definition: The number of heartbeats per minute; it counts the pump, not the breath.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟心跳次数；数的是泵，不是呼吸。

entries.definition: The volume of air moved per minute, a product of rate and tidal volume; it is not the breath count itself.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟移动的空气体积，等于频率乘潮气量，并不是呼吸次数本身。

entries.definition: The breathing process; adding rate makes it a quantity rather than an activity.
entries.definitionCN: 呼吸过程；加上 rate 之后，它变成一个量而非活动。

entries.definition: A plain-language equivalent of respiration rate, common in physiology and animal science.
entries.definitionCN: respiration rate 的通俗同义说法，常见于生理学与动物科学。

entries.definition: The total volume of air breathed per minute; it rises with rate but is measured in litres, not breaths.
entries.definitionCN: 每分钟吸入的空气总量；随频率上升，但以升计量，而非次数。

entries.definition: The palpable beat of the arteries, used as a quick check on heart rate rather than breathing.
entries.definitionCN: 可触及的动脉搏动，用来快速判断心率而非呼吸。

entries.definition: The air moved in one ordinary breath; paired with rate, it determines minute ventilation.
entries.definitionCN: 一次平常呼吸所移动的空气量；与频率配对决定每分通气量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: respiration + rate: breathing expressed as a count per minute.
normal.cn: respiration + rate：把呼吸表示成每分钟的次数。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: resting respiration rate, elevated respiration rate, normal respiration rate.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：静息呼吸频率、呼吸频率升高、正常呼吸频率。

normal.en: rate comes from Latin rata pars 'fixed portion', the same family as ratio and ration.
normal.cn: rate 出自拉丁 rata pars「固定份额」，与 ratio、ration 同族。

normal.en: Minute ventilation = respiration rate × tidal volume.
normal.cn: 每分通气量 = 呼吸频率 × 潮气量。

normal.en: Clinicians often say respiratory rate and write RR.
normal.cn: 临床医生常说 respiratory rate，并缩写为 RR。

abstract.en: Picture a stopwatch and a counting hand rising and falling with each chest movement.
abstract.cn: 想象一只秒表，与胸口起伏同步抬起落下的计数手指。

abstract.en: Picture a monitor beside a hospital bed showing a small green number for breaths.
abstract.cn: 想象病床旁的监护仪上，一个绿色小数字显示呼吸次数。

abstract.en: Picture a night-time chart with a line that dips whenever breathing slows.
abstract.cn: 想象一张夜间图表，呼吸变慢时曲线随之下沉。

examples.en: An adult's normal resting respiration rate is about twelve to twenty.
examples.cn: 成年人正常的静息呼吸频率约为每分钟十二到二十次。

examples.en: Fever and pain can raise the respiration rate.
examples.cn: 发热与疼痛会使呼吸频率升高。

examples.en: The monitor alarms when the respiration rate falls below eight.
examples.cn: 当呼吸频率低于八次时，监护仪会报警。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「respiration 呼吸 + rate 速率」——每分钟呼吸多少次 → respiration rate 呼吸频率

root: 拉丁 respiratio「呼吸」+ 英语 rate（出自拉丁 rata pars「固定份额」）→ 现代生理学复合词 respiration rate。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one number: a count of breaths per minute can be a baseline, an exertion value, a warning, a vital sign, an animal measure, a sleep record, a multiplier in ventilation, or a procedure for counting.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个数字展开：每分钟呼吸次数可以是基线值、运动值、警报、生命体征、动物指标、睡眠记录、通气量中的乘数，也可以是一套计数操作。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stopwatch beside a chest, turning each rise and fall into a count.
core.cn: 核心意象：胸旁的一只秒表，把每次起伏变成一个计数。

branches.en: THE NUMBER AND ITS MAKING: the rate is both a quantity and the procedure of counting that produces it.
branches.cn: 数字与制法：频率既是一个量，也是产生这个量的计数操作。

branches.en: TWO CONDITIONS: the same measure is taken at rest as a baseline and under effort as a load.
branches.cn: 两种状态：同一指标在静息时作为基线，在用力时作为负荷。

branches.en: THE CLINIC: deviation from the normal range turns the number into a warning and a vital sign.
branches.cn: 临床：偏离正常范围使这个数字变成警报与生命体征。

branches.en: OTHER BODIES AND OTHER HOURS: the measure travels to animals and to overnight sleep studies.
branches.cn: 别的身体与别的时段：这个指标延伸到动物，也延伸到整夜的睡眠监测。

branches.en: ONE FACTOR IN A PRODUCT: rate multiplied by tidal volume gives minute ventilation.
branches.cn: 乘积中的一个因子：频率乘以潮气量得到每分通气量。

intro.en: Respiration rate is a two-word compound: a Latin noun of breathing plus an English noun of reckoning.
intro.cn: respiration rate 是双词复合：一个拉丁「呼吸」名词加一个英语「计算」名词。

latinIntro.en: Respiratio comes from spirare 'to breathe'; rate comes from Latin rata pars, from reri 'to reckon', the same family as ratio and ration.
latinIntro.cn: respiratio 出自 spirare「呼吸」；rate 出自拉丁 rata pars，源于 reri「计算」，与 ratio、ration 同族。

items.meaningCN: 每分钟计数的呼吸次数
items.example: The respiration rate was recorded at eighteen.
items.exampleCN: 记录的呼吸频率是十八次。

items.meaning: the clinical wording of the same measure
items.meaningCN: 同一指标在临床上的说法
items.example: Respiratory rate is the fourth vital sign.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸频率是第四项生命体征。

items.example: Respiration supplies oxygen to tissues.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸为组织供氧。

items.example: Respiratory disease can alter the rate.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸系统疾病会改变呼吸频率。

items.example: The heart rate rose with fever.
items.exampleCN: 发热时心率上升。

items.example: The ratio of breaths to heartbeats is about one to four.
items.exampleCN: 呼吸与心跳之比约为四比一。

items.example: Each hiker carried a daily ration.
items.exampleCN: 每位徒步者携带一天的配给。

items.meaningCN: 一次呼吸移动的空气量
items.example: Tidal volume and rate together give minute ventilation.
items.exampleCN: 潮气量与频率一起得出每分通气量。

definition_zh: 循环的；血液循环的；循环系统的
definition_en: relating to the circulation of blood through the body, or to the system of heart and vessels that carries it
core_image: 一颗心脏连着满身血管，血液沿着环路不断绕行
scene: The circulatory system carries oxygen from the lungs to every tissue.
sceneCN: 这里 circulatory 指「循环系统的」（第 1 个义项：由心脏、血管与血液构成的整套循环结构）；句意：循环系统把氧气从肺运送到每一个组织。图中可辨识物件：心脏、动脉、静脉、毛细血管网。

pos.zh: 循环的；血液循环的；循环系统的

senses.title: Of the blood system
senses.titleCN: 循环系统的：心脏与血管组成的整体
senses.definition: belonging to the system of heart, blood and vessels that moves blood around the body
senses.definitionCN: 属于由心脏、血液与血管组成、把血液送往全身的系统
senses.example: The circulatory system carries oxygen from the lungs to every tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 循环系统把氧气从肺运送到每一个组织。
senses.why: Latin circulus 'small ring' gives the idea of moving around a closed loop; the adjective names that loop's machinery.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 circulus「小环」给出沿闭环运行的想法；这个形容词命名这套环路机制。

senses.title: Of blood movement
senses.titleCN: 血液循环的：血液在体内流动
senses.definition: connected with the movement of blood itself rather than with the organs
senses.definitionCN: 与血液本身的流动有关，而非与器官有关
senses.example: Cold hands show poor circulatory flow at the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 手发冷说明体表的血液循环不佳。
senses.why: The same adjective can describe the flow and the structures that produce it, a normal split in medical vocabulary.
senses.whyCN: 同一个形容词既可描述流动，也可描述产生流动的结构，这是医学术语中的常见分工。

senses.title: Of circulatory organs
senses.titleCN: 循环器官的：心脏与血管
senses.definition: describes the organs of circulation, chiefly the heart and the blood vessels
senses.definitionCN: 形容循环的器官，主要是心脏与血管
senses.example: Circulatory organs develop early in the embryo.
senses.exampleCN: 循环器官在胚胎早期就已发育。
senses.why: Anatomy attaches the adjective to the parts once the system is defined.
senses.whyCN: 一旦系统被定义，解剖学就把这个形容词附着在部件上。

senses.title: Circulatory disease
senses.titleCN: 循环系统疾病：影响心脏与血管的病症
senses.definition: describes illness of the heart and vessels, including high blood pressure and heart failure
senses.definitionCN: 形容心脏与血管的疾病，包括高血压与心力衰竭
senses.example: Circulatory disease is a leading cause of death worldwide.
senses.exampleCN: 循环系统疾病是世界范围内的主要死因之一。
senses.why: Epidemiology groups heart and vessel disorders under one adjective because they share risk factors and the same prevention.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学把心脏与血管的病症归在同一个形容词下，因为它们共享危险因素，也共享同一套预防手段。

senses.title: Circulatory failure
senses.titleCN: 循环衰竭：血液无法满足组织需要
senses.definition: a state in which blood flow is too weak to supply the body's tissues
senses.definitionCN: 血流过弱、无法供应身体组织的状态
senses.example: Circulatory failure after trauma requires urgent fluids.
senses.exampleCN: 创伤后的循环衰竭需要紧急补液。
senses.why: Failure is the point at which the loop can no longer supply the tissue, so the adjective marks the system's breakdown.
senses.whyCN: 衰竭是环路再也无法供应组织的那一点，因此这个形容词标记的是系统的崩溃。

senses.title: Of lymph and other fluids
senses.titleCN: 淋巴等体液循环的
senses.definition: broadly, relating to the movement of lymph or other body fluids, not only blood
senses.definitionCN: 广义上指淋巴或其他体液的流动，而非仅指血液
senses.example: Lymphatic vessels form a separate circulatory route.
senses.exampleCN: 淋巴管构成一条独立的循环路径。
senses.why: Physiology extended the adjective to the second circulation that returns tissue fluid to the blood.
senses.whyCN: 生理学把这个形容词扩展到第二条循环，即把组织液送回血液的系统。

senses.title: Of a closed loop
senses.titleCN: 环流的：沿闭合路径周而复始
senses.definition: describes any arrangement that moves material around a closed circuit
senses.definitionCN: 形容任何让物质沿闭合回路周而复始运动的安排
senses.example: The reactor uses a circulatory cooling loop.
senses.exampleCN: 该反应堆使用一套循环冷却回路。
senses.why: Engineering borrowed the ring image for pumps and pipes that recirculate a fluid.
senses.whyCN: 工程学借用「环」的意象，指让流体反复循环的泵与管道。

senses.title: The system as a noun
senses.titleCN: 循环系统（名词化用法）
senses.definition: rarely, the circulatory system taken as a noun phrase shortened to 'the circulatory'
senses.definitionCN: 罕用，指把 circulatory system 简称为 the circulatory
senses.example: The drug acts mainly on the circulatory.
senses.exampleCN: 这种药主要作用于循环系统。
senses.why: English often shortens the name of a system to its adjective with 'the', as with the digestive and the lymphatic.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把系统名称简化为「the + 形容词」，如 the digestive、the lymphatic。

intro.en: Circulatory comes from Latin circulatorius, built on circulari 'to carry around', from circulus 'small ring', a diminutive of circus 'ring'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: circulatory 出自拉丁 circulatorius，由 circulari「环绕运送」构成，而 circulus「小环」是 circus「环」的指小形式。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Circus named a ring, especially the round arena for races. From it came circulus, a small ring or circle.
items.cn: circus 指环，尤其是举行赛跑的圆形竞技场。由它产生 circulus，即小环或圆圈。

items.en: Circulari meant 'to form a circle, to move round'. Classical Latin used it for things going around rather than for blood.
items.cn: circulari 意为「成环、绕行」。古典拉丁用它指事物绕圈，而非血液。

items.en: William Harvey's demonstration of the circulation of the blood in 1628 gave the ring image its medical centre; the word circulation was extended from there.
items.cn: 1628 年哈维证明血液循环，使「环」的意象获得医学核心；circulation 一词由此扩展。

items.en: English circulatory appears in the seventeenth century, first in medical writing about the movement of blood.
items.cn: 英语 circulatory 于 17 世纪出现，最早见于关于血液运动的医学写作。

items.en: Later physiology and engineering applied the adjective to lymphatic flow and to any closed loop of pumped fluid.
items.cn: 后来的生理学与工程学把这个形容词用于淋巴流动，也用于任何泵送流体的闭合回路。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first English citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of Latin circus is disputed; any Indo-European form behind it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：英语最早书证年代存疑；拉丁 circus 的更深来源有争议，其背后的任何印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same Latin family that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the blood system and its flow.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词族、容易混淆的词；第二组是「血液系统及其流动」的近义词。

entries.definition: The movement of blood or the flow of anything through a loop; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液运动或任何事物沿环路的流动；形容词描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: To move around a loop or to spread; it names the action, not a structure.
entries.definitionCN: 沿环路运动或传播；它命名动作，而非结构。

entries.definition: A pump or person that keeps something moving around; a countable noun.
entries.definitionCN: 让某物持续环流的泵或人；是可数名词。

entries.definition: Means 'round in shape' or 'going in a circle of reasoning'; it does not name the blood system.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「圆形的」或「循环论证的」，并不指血液系统。

entries.definition: Relating to blood vessels; circulatory also includes the heart and the blood itself.
entries.definitionCN: 与血管有关；circulatory 还包括心脏与血液本身。

entries.definition: Relating specifically to the heart and vessels, the core of the circulatory system.
entries.definitionCN: 专指心脏与血管，即循环系统的核心。

entries.definition: Relating to blood as a tissue; it does not by itself mean the pump-and-pipe system.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为组织的血液有关，本身并不指泵与管道的系统。

entries.definition: Relating to the pressures and flows of blood; it describes physics, not anatomy.
entries.definitionCN: 与血液的压力与流动有关，描述物理而非解剖。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: circulus 'small ring' + -atory: the machinery of a closed loop.
normal.cn: circulus「小环」+ -atory：闭合环路的机制。

normal.en: The family runs circulate, circulation, circulator and circular.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 circulate、circulation、circulator、circular。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: circulatory system, circulatory disease, circulatory failure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：循环系统、循环系统疾病、循环衰竭。

normal.en: Harvey's 1628 work on the circulation of blood fixed the medical image of the ring.
normal.cn: 哈维 1628 年关于血液循环的工作固定了「环」的医学意象。

normal.en: vascular names the pipes; cardiovascular names the pump and pipes together.
normal.cn: vascular 指管道，cardiovascular 指泵与管道一起。

abstract.en: Picture a racetrack whose lanes are blood vessels and whose start line is the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一条跑道，跑道是血管，起跑线是心脏。

abstract.en: Picture a city ring road on which traffic never stops and never exits.
abstract.cn: 想象一条城市环路，车流从不停下也从不驶出。

abstract.en: Picture a pump in a basement sending water around a sealed loop of pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象地下室里一台泵，把水送进一圈密封管道。

examples.en: The circulatory system includes the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries.
examples.cn: 循环系统包括心脏、动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

examples.en: Shock is a circulatory problem before it is anything else.
examples.cn: 休克首先是一个循环问题。

examples.en: The reactor's circulatory loop is checked every month.
examples.cn: 反应堆的循环回路每月检查一次。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「circul 圈 + atory 的」——沿着圈不停转的 → circulatory 循环的

root: 拉丁 circus「环」→ circulus「小环」→ circulari「环绕」→ 拉丁 circulatorius → 英语 circulatory。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: blood runs around a closed ring, and that ring can be named as a system, as a flow, as organs, as a disease, as a failure, as a second fluid, or as any engineered loop.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：血液沿闭合的环运行，而这个环可被命名为系统、流动、器官、疾病、衰竭、第二种体液，或任何人工回路。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: blood running around a closed ring whose pump is the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：血液沿一个闭合的环运行，泵是心脏。

branches.en: THE SYSTEM AND ITS PARTS: the whole ring and the organs that make it run.
branches.cn: 系统与部件：整套环路以及让它运转的器官。

branches.en: FLOW AND LOOP: the movement itself, whether inside a body or inside an engine.
branches.cn: 流动与回路：运动本身，不论发生在身体里还是机器里。

branches.en: WHEN THE RING BREAKS: disease weakens it, and failure stops its supply.
branches.cn: 当环断裂：疾病削弱它，衰竭则让它停止供应。

branches.en: THE SECOND CIRCULATION: lymph returns tissue fluid by a parallel route.
branches.cn: 第二条循环：淋巴沿一条平行路径把组织液送回。

branches.en: SHORTENED NOUN: the system can be named by the adjective alone.
branches.cn: 名词化简称：整套系统可以只用形容词来指称。

intro.en: Circulatory is a Latin verb of going around plus the functional adjective suffix -ory: circulat- + -ory.
intro.cn: circulatory 是拉丁「环绕」动词加功能形容词后缀 -ory：circulat- + -ory。

latinIntro.en: Latin circulus 'small ring' gives circulare and circulatorius, hence English circulate, circulation, circulator, circulatory and circular.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 circulus「小环」产生 circulare 与 circulatorius，因此有英语 circulate、circulation、circulator、circulatory、circular。

items.meaning: relating to movement around a loop
items.example: Circulatory support kept the patient alive.
items.exampleCN: 循环支持维持了病人的生命。

items.meaning: to move around a loop; to spread
items.example: Blood circulates through the lungs.
items.exampleCN: 血液流经肺部循环。

items.example: Poor circulation makes the feet cold.
items.exampleCN: 循环不佳使双脚发冷。

items.meaning: a pump or person that keeps fluid moving
items.meaningCN: 让流体持续循环的泵或人
items.example: The heater has a small circulator.
items.exampleCN: 这台取暖器有一个小循环泵。

items.example: A circular argument returns to its start.
items.exampleCN: 循环论证又回到起点。

items.example: The Latin word circulus means a little ring.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁词 circulus 意为小环。

items.example: The Roman circus was a racetrack.
items.exampleCN: 罗马的 circus 是一条赛马场。

items.meaning: the heart, vessels and blood taken together
items.meaningCN: 心脏、血管与血液的整体
items.example: The circulatory system is closed in vertebrates.
items.exampleCN: 脊椎动物的循环系统是闭合的。

latinEntries.meaning: to form a circle, to move round

definition_zh: 心血管的；心血管系统的
definition_en: relating to the heart and the blood vessels, especially as a single system
core_image: 一颗心脏连着动脉与静脉网络，构成一套封闭的输送系统
scene: Regular exercise lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease.
sceneCN: 这里 cardiovascular 指「心血管的」（第 1 个义项：同时涉及心脏与血管）；句意：规律运动降低心血管疾病的风险。图中可辨识物件：心脏、冠状动脉、动脉树、跑步鞋。

pos.zh: 心血管的；心血管系统的（同时涉及心脏与血管）

collocations.zh: 心血管事件（如心梗、中风）

senses.title: Heart and vessels together
senses.titleCN: 心血管的：同时涉及心脏与血管
senses.definition: relating to the heart and the blood vessels considered as one system
senses.definitionCN: 指同时涉及作为单一系统的心脏与血管
senses.example: Regular exercise lowers the risk of cardiovascular disease.
senses.exampleCN: 规律运动降低心血管疾病的风险。
senses.why: The word joins Greek kardia 'heart' to Latin vasculum 'small vessel', naming the two halves of one loop.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把希腊 kardia「心脏」与拉丁 vasculum「小血管」连接起来，命名同一个环的两半。

senses.title: The cardiovascular system
senses.titleCN: 心血管系统：泵与管道构成的整体
senses.definition: the heart, arteries, veins and capillaries taken as a single transport system
senses.definitionCN: 把心脏、动脉、静脉与毛细血管视为一套输送系统
senses.example: The cardiovascular system is closed in mammals.
senses.exampleCN: 哺乳动物的心血管系统是闭合的。
senses.why: Medicine prefers one adjective for the pump-and-pipe unit, because diseases rarely respect the boundary.
senses.whyCN: 医学偏爱用一个形容词指「泵加管道」的整体，因为疾病很少尊重这条分界。

senses.title: Cardiovascular disease
senses.titleCN: 心血管疾病：心梗、中风、高血压等
senses.definition: the group of disorders of the heart and vessels, including heart attack, stroke and hypertension
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与血管疾病的总称，包括心梗、中风与高血压
senses.example: Cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of death globally.
senses.exampleCN: 心血管疾病仍是全球首要死因。
senses.why: Epidemiology needed a single label to group conditions that share risk factors and prevention.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学需要一个统一标签，把共享危险因素与预防手段的病症归为一组。

senses.title: Cardiovascular health
senses.titleCN: 心血管健康：系统的功能状态
senses.definition: the general condition of the heart and vessels, measured by pressure, lipids and fitness
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与血管的整体状况，由血压、血脂与体能衡量
senses.example: Diet and sleep both shape cardiovascular health.
senses.exampleCN: 饮食与睡眠都影响心血管健康。
senses.why: Prevention language needed a positive label, so the adjective came to name the state to be protected, not only the disease to be avoided.
senses.whyCN: 预防语汇需要一个正面标签，于是这个形容词开始命名需要被保护的状态，而不只是要避免的疾病。

senses.title: Cardiovascular fitness
senses.titleCN: 心血管适能：持续运动的能力
senses.definition: the ability of the heart and lungs to supply oxygen during sustained exercise
senses.definitionCN: 心脏与肺在持续运动中供应氧气的能力
senses.example: Running builds cardiovascular fitness faster than walking.
senses.exampleCN: 跑步比走路更快提升心血管适能。
senses.why: Sports science borrowed the medical adjective for the endurance side of training, later shortened to cardio.
senses.whyCN: 运动科学借用了医学形容词指训练的耐力面，后来缩略为 cardio。

senses.title: Cardiovascular risk
senses.titleCN: 心血管风险：发生事件的概率
senses.definition: the estimated probability of a heart attack, stroke or other vascular event
senses.definitionCN: 发生心梗、中风或其他血管事件的估计概率
senses.example: Smoking doubles cardiovascular risk in young adults.
senses.exampleCN: 吸烟使年轻人的心血管风险翻倍。
senses.why: Risk turns the system into a probability, estimated from pressure, lipids and smoking rather than observed directly.
senses.whyCN: 风险把系统变成一个概率，它由血压、血脂与吸烟估算而来，而非直接观察。

senses.title: Cardiovascular event
senses.titleCN: 心血管事件：突发的临床发作
senses.definition: a sudden clinical occurrence such as a heart attack or stroke
senses.definitionCN: 突发的临床发作，如心肌梗死或中风
senses.example: The trial counted every cardiovascular event over five years.
senses.exampleCN: 该试验统计了五年内每一次心血管事件。
senses.why: Trials count discrete occurrences, so the adjective attaches to 'event' as the unit of outcome.
senses.whyCN: 试验统计的是一次次离散的发生，因此这个形容词附着在 event 上，作为结局的单位。

senses.title: Cardiovascular drugs and surgery
senses.titleCN: 心血管药物与手术的
senses.definition: describes treatments aimed at the heart and vessels, such as stents or blood-pressure drugs
senses.definitionCN: 形容针对心脏与血管的治疗，如支架或降压药
senses.example: Cardiovascular surgery replaced two blocked arteries.
senses.exampleCN: 心血管手术替换了两条堵塞的动脉。
senses.why: Treatment language attaches the adjective to what is done to the pump and pipes, not to what they are.
senses.whyCN: 治疗语汇把这个形容词附着在「对泵与管道做了什么」上，而不是它们本身是什么。

intro.en: Cardiovascular is a hybrid compound: Greek kardia 'heart' plus Latin vasculum 'small vessel', joined by the combining vowel -o-. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: cardiovascular 是混合复合词：希腊 kardia「心脏」加拉丁 vasculum「小血管」，由连接元音 -o- 结合。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Kardia meant 'heart' both as an organ and as the seat of feeling. It gives English cardiac, cardiology and the prefix cardio-.
items.cn: kardia 既指作为器官的心脏，也指情感的所在。它产生英语 cardiac、cardiology 与前缀 cardio-。

items.en: Vas meant 'vessel, container'; its diminutive vasculum meant 'small vessel', and vascularis gave English vascular.
items.cn: vas 意为「容器、器皿」；其指小形式 vasculum 意为「小容器」，vascularis 给出英语 vascular。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine often joined a Greek prefix to a Latin stem, because both languages already supplied the technical vocabulary.
items.cn: 19 世纪医学常把希腊前缀与拉丁词干拼接，因为两种语言都已提供了专业词汇。

items.en: Cardiovascular is recorded in the late nineteenth century, around the 1870s. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: cardiovascular 记录于 19 世纪后期，约在 1870 年代。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Twentieth-century epidemiology made cardiovascular disease a standard category and later shortened the fitness sense to cardio.
items.cn: 20 世纪流行病学使 cardiovascular disease 成为标准类别，后来又把体能义缩略为 cardio。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact date of the coinage is uncertain, and the deeper origins of both kardia and vas are reconstructions rather than recorded words.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：该词的确切造词年代存疑；kardia 与 vas 的更深来源均属重构形式，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds words that name one half of the compound or a neighbour; the second holds near-synonyms for the same system and its health.
note.cn: 第一组是指称复合词某一半或相邻概念的词；第二组是「同一系统及其健康」的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating only to the heart, as in cardiac arrest; cardiovascular also covers the vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指心脏，如心脏停搏；cardiovascular 还包括血管。

entries.definition: Relating only to blood vessels; it omits the pump.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指血管，不含泵。

entries.definition: Informal shorthand for cardiovascular exercise, not for the medical adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 口语中是有氧运动的简称，不是医学形容词的替代。

entries.definition: The branch of medicine dealing with the heart; the adjective describes patients and risks, not the discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 研究心脏的医学分支；形容词描述病人与风险，不指学科。

entries.definition: Relating to the whole blood circuit, including the blood itself; cardiovascular stresses heart and vessels.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个血液环路，包括血液本身；cardiovascular 强调心脏与血管。

entries.definition: Relating to the arteries that supply the heart muscle; it is narrower than cardiovascular.
entries.definitionCN: 指供应心肌的动脉，比 cardiovascular 范围窄。

entries.definition: Relating to the heart and lungs, a pairing used for resuscitation and fitness testing.
entries.definitionCN: 指心脏与肺，用于复苏与体能测试。

entries.definition: Relating to hardening and plaque in arteries, one mechanism within cardiovascular disease.
entries.definitionCN: 指动脉硬化与斑块形成，是心血管疾病中的一种机制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cardio- 'heart' + vascular 'vessels': the pump and the pipes named together.
normal.cn: cardio-「心脏」+ vascular「血管」：泵与管道一起命名。

normal.en: The family runs cardiac, cardiology, cardiologist, vascular and cardiopulmonary.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cardiac、cardiology、cardiologist、vascular、cardiopulmonary。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: cardiovascular disease, cardiovascular risk, cardiovascular event.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：心血管疾病、心血管风险、心血管事件。

normal.en: The gym word cardio is a shortening of cardiovascular exercise.
normal.cn: 健身房里的 cardio 是 cardiovascular exercise 的缩略。

normal.en: cardiac is only the heart; vascular is only the vessels.
normal.cn: cardiac 只指心脏，vascular 只指血管。

abstract.en: Picture a pump with red and blue pipes branching through a whole body.
abstract.cn: 想象一台泵，红色与蓝色管道布满全身。

abstract.en: Picture a treadmill readout showing heart rate and oxygen use together.
abstract.cn: 想象跑步机的读数同时显示心率与耗氧量。

abstract.en: Picture a plaque narrowing a coronary artery like sediment in a pipe.
abstract.cn: 想象斑块像管道里的沉积物一样把冠状动脉收窄。

examples.en: Cardiovascular disease accounts for about a third of deaths worldwide.
examples.cn: 心血管疾病约占全球死亡人数的三分之一。

examples.en: Thirty minutes of cardiovascular exercise five times a week is a common target.
examples.cn: 每周五次、每次三十分钟的有氧运动是常见目标。

examples.en: The study tracked cardiovascular events over ten years.
examples.cn: 该研究追踪了十年间的心血管事件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cardio 心 + vascular 血管」——心脏加血管 → cardiovascular 心血管的

root: 希腊 kardia「心脏」+ 拉丁 vasculum「小血管」→ 19 世纪医学混合复合词 cardiovascular。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one system: the heart and its pipes can be named together, then measured as health, fitness, risk, event, and finally as a target of drugs and surgery.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个系统展开：心脏与管道可以一起命名，随后被衡量为健康、适能、风险、事件，最后成为药物与手术的靶点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pump and a branching network of pipes serving one closed loop.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台泵与一套分叉管道，服务同一个闭合环路。

branches.en: THE UNIT: the compound exists to name heart and vessels as one thing.
branches.cn: 整体单元：这个复合词的存在，就是把心脏与血管命名为一件事。

branches.en: THE CLINICAL FACE: disease is the negative measure of the same system's health.
branches.cn: 临床面孔：疾病是同一系统健康的反向度量。

branches.en: THE TRAINING FACE: fitness asks how much oxygen the system can deliver under load.
branches.cn: 训练面孔：适能问的是系统在负荷下能输送多少氧气。

branches.en: PROBABILITY AND EVENT: risk is the forecast, an event is the occurrence.
branches.cn: 概率与事件：风险是预测，事件是实际发生。

branches.en: THE TARGET: drugs and surgery address the same pump and pipes.
branches.cn: 靶点：药物与手术处理的仍是同一台泵与同一套管道。

intro.en: Cardiovascular is a Greek heart stem plus a Latin vessel adjective, a hybrid typical of scientific English.
intro.cn: cardiovascular 是希腊「心脏」词干加拉丁「血管」形容词，是科学英语常见的混合构造。

latinIntro.en: Greek kardia supplies cardiac, cardiology and cardio-; Latin vas and vasculum supply vascular and vasculature.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 kardia 提供 cardiac、cardiology 与 cardio-；拉丁 vas 与 vasculum 提供 vascular 与 vasculature。

items.meaning: relating to the heart and vessels
items.example: Cardiovascular health depends on blood pressure.
items.exampleCN: 心血管健康取决于血压。

items.example: Cardiac muscle contracts rhythmically.
items.exampleCN: 心肌有节律地收缩。

items.example: She trained in cardiology for four years.
items.exampleCN: 她接受了四年心脏病学训练。

items.example: The cardiologist ordered an angiogram.
items.exampleCN: 心脏科医生安排了血管造影。

items.example: Vascular tissue carries water in plants.
items.exampleCN: 维管组织在植物中输送水分。

items.meaning: the vessel network of an organ
items.example: The tumour has a dense vasculature.
items.exampleCN: 这个肿瘤血管网络密集。

items.example: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation restores breathing and circulation.
items.exampleCN: 心肺复苏恢复呼吸与循环。

items.meaningCN: 健身语境中的有氧运动
items.example: She does forty minutes of cardio daily.
items.exampleCN: 她每天做四十分钟有氧运动。

definition_en: a tube in the body through which blood flows, such as an artery, vein or capillary
core_image: 体内一条细管，管壁内血液单向流动
scene: A blocked blood vessel in the brain can cause a stroke.
sceneCN: 这里 blood vessel 指「血管」（第 1 个义项：血液在体内流动的管道总称）；句意：脑内一条血管堵塞可能引发中风。图中可辨识物件：脑血管、血栓、脑部扫描、导管。

pos.zh: 血管（动脉、静脉与毛细血管的总称；可数）

forms.label: 小血管
forms.form: blood vessel 的指小说法为 arteriole（小动脉）、venule（小静脉）

forms.label: 近义复合词
forms.form: blood vessel 与 blood-vessel（连字符形式）并存

senses.title: Any vessel carrying blood
senses.titleCN: 血管：运送血液的管道总称
senses.definition: a tube of any size through which blood is carried around the body
senses.definitionCN: 体内任何尺寸、用来运送血液的管道
senses.example: Blood vessels branch smaller and smaller as they reach the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 血管到达组织时越分越细。
senses.why: The compound simply names the container and its content: a vessel for blood.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词只是命名容器及其内容：装血的管子。

senses.title: An artery
senses.titleCN: 动脉：把血从心脏送出的血管
senses.definition: specifically, a vessel that carries blood away from the heart
senses.definitionCN: 特指把血液从心脏送出的血管
senses.example: The aorta is the largest blood vessel in the body.
senses.exampleCN: 主动脉是体内最大的血管。
senses.why: Anatomy divides the general word by direction of flow, and arteries are one half of that division.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学按血流方向划分这个通称，动脉是这一划分的一半。

senses.title: A vein
senses.titleCN: 静脉：把血送回心脏的血管
senses.definition: specifically, a vessel that carries blood back toward the heart
senses.definitionCN: 特指把血液送回心脏的血管
senses.example: A cut vein bleeds steadily rather than spurting.
senses.exampleCN: 静脉被割破后是持续渗血，而不是喷射。
senses.why: The return route is named by the same general term with a different qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 回流路径用同一个通称加不同限定来命名。

senses.title: A capillary
senses.titleCN: 毛细血管：气体与养分交换处
senses.definition: the smallest blood vessel, where exchange with tissue fluid takes place
senses.definitionCN: 最小的血管，与组织液进行物质交换的地方
senses.example: Oxygen crosses the wall of a capillary into the tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 氧气穿过毛细血管壁进入组织。
senses.why: The compound covers the finest branches too, where the tube becomes a permeable wall.
senses.whyCN: 这个通称也涵盖最细的分支，此时管道变成一层可渗透的壁。

senses.title: The vessel wall
senses.titleCN: 血管壁：管壁结构与弹性
senses.definition: the layered wall of a vessel, whose muscle and lining control flow
senses.definitionCN: 血管的分层管壁，其肌肉与内膜控制流动
senses.example: Cholesterol builds up inside a blood vessel wall.
senses.exampleCN: 胆固醇在血管壁内堆积。
senses.why: The physical tube has its own anatomy, so the phrase can name the wall rather than the lumen.
senses.whyCN: 这条实体管道自有解剖结构，因此这个短语也可指管壁而非管腔。

senses.title: Diseased vessel
senses.titleCN: 病变血管：堵塞、破裂或变窄
senses.definition: a vessel affected by blockage, rupture, inflammation or abnormal widening
senses.definitionCN: 受堵塞、破裂、炎症或异常扩张影响的血管
senses.example: A blocked blood vessel in the brain can cause a stroke.
senses.exampleCN: 脑内一条血管堵塞可能引发中风。
senses.why: Clinical writing uses the phrase as the site of pathology, not just as normal anatomy.
senses.whyCN: 临床写作把这个短语当作病变部位，而不只是正常解剖。

senses.title: The vessel network
senses.titleCN: 血管网络：器官内的整体分布
senses.definition: the whole arrangement of vessels supplying an organ or region
senses.definitionCN: 供应某个器官或区域的全部血管分布
senses.example: The liver has a dense blood vessel network.
senses.exampleCN: 肝脏有密集的血管网络。
senses.why: The count noun extends to the collective pattern, a shift from one tube to the system.
senses.whyCN: 可数名词扩展到整体格局，从一根管子转到整个系统。

senses.title: Vessel imaging
senses.titleCN: 血管成像：造影与超声检查
senses.definition: in medicine, the object visualized by angiography or ultrasound
senses.definitionCN: 医学中经血管造影或超声显像的对象
senses.example: The scan showed a narrow blood vessel near the heart.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描显示心脏附近有一条狭窄的血管。
senses.why: Radiology needed the phrase as the object of the image, because with contrast the vessel itself becomes visible.
senses.whyCN: 放射学需要这个短语作为成像的对象，因为使用造影剂后血管本身变得可见。

senses.title: New vessel growth
senses.titleCN: 血管新生：组织长出新血管
senses.definition: the formation of new vessels, as in healing, tumour growth or exercise adaptation
senses.definitionCN: 新血管的形成，见于愈合、肿瘤生长或运动适应
senses.example: Tumours release signals that trigger new blood vessel growth.
senses.exampleCN: 肿瘤释放信号，触发新血管生长。
senses.why: Research on angiogenesis made the phrase a target of drugs that starve tumours.
senses.whyCN: 血管生成研究使这个短语成为「饿死肿瘤」药物的靶点。

intro.en: Blood vessel is a native English compound: blood from Old English blod, vessel from Old French vaissel, ultimately Latin vascellum 'small container'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: blood vessel 是英语本族复合词：blood 出自古英语 blod，vessel 经古法语 vaissel 上溯拉丁 vascellum「小容器」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Blod names blood and belongs to the native Germanic vocabulary; its deeper Indo-European connections are reconstructed, not recorded.
items.cn: blod 指血，属本族日耳曼词汇；其更深的印欧语联系属重构，并无记录。

items.en: Vas 'container' had the diminutive vascellum or vasculum 'small vessel', which passed through Old French vaissel into English vessel.
items.cn: vas「容器」的指小形式 vascellum 或 vasculum 意为「小容器」，经古法语 vaissel 进入英语 vessel。

items.en: The compound blood vessel is recorded in the fourteenth century, when anatomy needed a plain term for the tubes carrying blood.
items.cn: blood vessel 这一复合词记录于 14 世纪，当时解剖学需要为运血的管道找一个平实说法。

items.en: The seventeenth-century discovery of the circulation gave the phrase a fixed place in physiology, dividing vessels by direction of flow.
items.cn: 17 世纪发现血液循环，使这个短语在生理学中固定下来，并按血流方向划分血管。

items.en: Twentieth-century surgery and cancer research added phrases such as blood vessel formation and blood vessel wall.
items.cn: 20 世纪的外科学与癌症研究加入了 blood vessel formation、blood vessel wall 等说法。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origin of both blod and vas is reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与更深词根）：最早书证年代存疑；blod 与 vas 的更深来源均属重构，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds the specific vessel types and the easily confused near-forms; the second holds broader terms for the vessel system.
note.cn: 第一组是具体的血管类型与易混近形词；第二组是血管系统的上位说法。

entries.definition: The blood flowing through the vessels; it names the content, while blood vessel names the container.
entries.definitionCN: 指在血管中流动的血液，命名内容物；blood vessel 命名容器。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood away from the heart; it is a type of blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管，是血管的一种。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood back to the heart; the other main type of blood vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 把血送回心脏的血管，是血管的另一主要类型。

entries.definition: The smallest vessel, where exchange with tissue occurs.
entries.definitionCN: 最小的血管，与组织进行物质交换。

entries.definition: The collection of vessels in an organ or body; it is collective, while a blood vessel is countable.
entries.definitionCN: 某个器官或全身的血管集合，是集合名词；blood vessel 则可数。

entries.definition: The whole set of vessels taken as an anatomical system.
entries.definitionCN: 把全部血管视为一个解剖系统。

entries.definition: A small branch of an artery, too large to be a capillary.
entries.definitionCN: 动脉的小分支，比毛细血管大。

entries.definition: A small vein that collects blood from capillaries.
entries.definitionCN: 从毛细血管收集血液的小静脉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: blood + vessel: a container for blood, exactly as the two words say.
normal.cn: blood + vessel：装血的容器，两个词字面就说清了。

normal.en: vessel comes from Latin vascellum 'small container', the same root as vascular.
normal.cn: vessel 出自拉丁 vascellum「小容器」，与 vascular 同根。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: blocked blood vessel, blood vessel wall, burst blood vessel.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：堵塞的血管、血管壁、血管破裂。

normal.en: The three types are artery, vein and capillary.
normal.cn: 三种类型是动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

normal.en: bloodstream is the contents; blood vessel is the tube.
normal.cn: bloodstream 是内容物，blood vessel 是管道。

abstract.en: Picture a branching river system inside the body, with the heart as its source.
abstract.cn: 想象体内一套分叉的河流系统，心脏是源头。

abstract.en: Picture a pipe narrowing until its wall becomes thin enough for oxygen to slip through.
abstract.cn: 想象管道不断变窄，管壁薄到氧气能穿过去。

abstract.en: Picture a scan lighting up a single narrow channel beside a beating heart.
abstract.cn: 想象扫描图上，跳动的心脏旁亮起一条狭窄通道。

examples.en: Damaged blood vessels in the retina can blur vision.
examples.cn: 视网膜受损的血管会使视力模糊。

examples.en: Exercise improves blood vessel function within a few weeks.
examples.cn: 运动在几周内就能改善血管功能。

examples.en: The surgeon grafted a healthy blood vessel onto the blocked artery.
examples.cn: 外科医生把一段健康血管接到堵塞的动脉上。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blood 血 + vessel 容器」——装血的容器 → blood vessel 血管

root: 古英语 blod「血」+ 古法语 vaissel（拉丁 vascellum「小容器」）→ 英语复合词 blood vessel。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one tube: blood runs through it, and that tube can be classified by direction, narrowed to the smallest branch, examined in its wall, diseased, counted as a network, imaged, or newly grown.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一根管子展开：血液流过它，而这根管子可按方向分类、缩小到最细分支、细看管壁、成为病灶、作为网络计数、被成像，或新长出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tube inside the body with blood moving along it.
core.cn: 核心意象：体内一根管子，血液沿它流动。

branches.en: THREE NAMED FORMS: artery, vein and capillary are the specialised types of tube.
branches.cn: 三种专名：动脉、静脉与毛细血管是管道的专门形态。

branches.en: THE PHYSICAL TUBE: the wall that can thicken, and the vessel that can block or burst.
branches.cn: 实体管道：可以增厚的管壁，以及会堵塞或破裂的血管。

branches.en: THE NETWORK AND THE IMAGE: many tubes taken together, and the same tubes seen on a scan.
branches.cn: 网络与影像：多根管子合起来看，以及同一批管子在扫描图上的样子。

branches.en: NEW TUBES: healing and tumours both build vessels, which makes the phrase a drug target.
branches.cn: 新管子：愈合与肿瘤都会造血管，这使该短语成为药物靶点。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER LOGIC: vessel means container, so the compound never means the blood itself.
branches.cn: 容器逻辑：vessel 意为容器，因此这个复合词从不指血液本身。

intro.en: Blood vessel is a native compound of a Germanic word for blood and a Latin-derived word for container.
intro.cn: blood vessel 是「日耳曼语的血」与「拉丁来源的容器」构成的本族复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vas 'container' gives vascellum, vasculum, vascular and vasculature; English vessel arrived through Old French vaissel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vas「容器」产生 vascellum、vasculum、vascular、vasculature；英语 vessel 经古法语 vaissel 进入。

items.example: The clot blocked a small blood vessel.
items.exampleCN: 血栓堵住了一条小血管。

items.example: Vascular disease narrows the arteries.
items.exampleCN: 血管疾病使动脉变窄。

items.example: The skin has a rich vasculature.
items.exampleCN: 皮肤有丰富的血管网络。

items.example: The graft vascularized within weeks.
items.exampleCN: 移植物在几周内形成了血管。

items.example: Poor vascularization slows healing.
items.exampleCN: 血管形成不良会延缓愈合。

items.example: Angiogenesis feeds a growing tumour.
items.exampleCN: 血管生成供养不断长大的肿瘤。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood away from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The carotid artery supplies the brain.
items.exampleCN: 颈动脉供应大脑。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood back to the heart
items.example: The vein was used for the drip.
items.exampleCN: 这条静脉被用来输液。

definition_zh: 血流；血液循环；（体内的）血液
definition_en: the blood flowing through the body's vessels, considered as one continuous stream
core_image: 血液在全身血管里像一条河流一样不断流动
scene: The drug reaches the bloodstream within twenty minutes.
sceneCN: 这里 bloodstream 指「血液循环」（第 3 个义项：进入并在全身血流中运行）；句意：药物在二十分钟内进入血液循环。图中可辨识物件：血管剖面、药片、血流箭头、计时器。

pos.zh: 血流；血液循环；体内的血液（通常作单数，前面加 the）

forms.label: 复数（少见）
forms.form: bloodstreams（仅在比喻多个循环系统时使用）

forms.label: 通常形式
forms.form: the bloodstream（多作单数集合名词）

senses.title: The circulating blood
senses.titleCN: 血液循环：体内不断流动的血液整体
senses.definition: the blood moving continuously through the arteries, veins and capillaries
senses.definitionCN: 在动脉、静脉与毛细血管中持续流动的血液整体
senses.example: The heart keeps the bloodstream moving day and night.
senses.exampleCN: 心脏让血液循环日夜不停。
senses.why: The compound joins blood to stream, picturing the whole circulation as one river rather than separate vessels.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 blood 与 stream 结合，把整套循环想象成一条河，而不是一根根分开的管子。

senses.title: The blood as a medium
senses.titleCN: 血液：作为运输介质的体液
senses.definition: the blood regarded as the medium that carries oxygen, nutrients, hormones and waste
senses.definitionCN: 把血液看作运送氧气、养分、激素与废物的介质
senses.example: Glucose dissolves in the bloodstream and is carried to cells.
senses.exampleCN: 葡萄糖溶在血液中，被送到细胞。
senses.why: Once pictured as a stream, the blood becomes a medium in which things dissolve and travel.
senses.whyCN: 一旦被想象成河流，血液就变成一种可以把东西溶入并带走的介质。

senses.title: Entering the circulation
senses.titleCN: 进入血液循环：药物或养分入血
senses.definition: the route by which a substance passes into the circulating blood
senses.definitionCN: 物质进入循环血液的途径
senses.example: The drug reaches the bloodstream within twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 药物在二十分钟内进入血液循环。
senses.why: Pharmacology needs a destination phrase, and 'the bloodstream' names the compartment a substance must reach to act.
senses.whyCN: 药理学需要一个「目的地」说法，而 the bloodstream 正是物质要到达才能起效的隔室。

senses.title: Concentration in blood
senses.titleCN: 血中浓度：血液里某物的水平
senses.definition: the level of a substance present in the circulating blood at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时刻循环血液中某物质的水平
senses.example: Insulin levels in the bloodstream rise after a meal.
senses.exampleCN: 饭后血液中的胰岛素水平升高。
senses.why: Measurement made the stream a sampling site, so the word appears in phrases about levels and concentrations.
senses.whyCN: 测量让这条「河流」成为取样点，因此这个词出现在关于水平与浓度的短语中。

senses.title: Spread through blood
senses.titleCN: 经血流传播：感染或细胞随血扩散
senses.definition: the route by which infection, toxins or cancer cells travel around the body
senses.definitionCN: 感染、毒素或癌细胞在全身扩散的途径
senses.example: Bacteria in the bloodstream can cause sepsis.
senses.exampleCN: 血液中的细菌可能引发败血症。
senses.why: Because the stream reaches every tissue, it becomes the body's highway for harm as well as for supply.
senses.whyCN: 因为这条「河流」到达每个组织，它既是供应线，也是伤害的通道。

senses.title: Bloodstream infection
senses.titleCN: 血流感染：血液中出现病原体
senses.definition: a clinical condition in which microorganisms are present and growing in the blood
senses.definitionCN: 微生物在血液中存在并繁殖的临床状态
senses.example: A bloodstream infection requires immediate antibiotics.
senses.exampleCN: 血流感染需要立即使用抗生素。
senses.why: Microbiology needed a compartment name to say where the organisms are growing, and the stream supplied one.
senses.whyCN: 微生物学需要一个隔室名称来说明病原体在哪里繁殖，而 bloodstream 正好提供了这样一个名称。

senses.title: Flow and speed
senses.titleCN: 血流速度：循环的快慢
senses.definition: the rate at which blood moves through the circulation as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 血液在整个循环中移动的快慢
senses.example: Exercise speeds up the bloodstream and warms the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 运动加快血流并使皮肤变暖。
senses.why: Stream carries the idea of current, so the word can describe rate as well as contents.
senses.whyCN: stream 带有「水流」之意，因此这个词既可指内容物，也可指流速。

senses.title: Everything carried in blood
senses.titleCN: 血液运载物：氧气、糖、激素与废物
senses.definition: the set of substances in transit in the blood at any moment
senses.definitionCN: 任一时刻在血液中运输的全部物质
senses.example: The bloodstream carries carbon dioxide back to the lungs.
senses.exampleCN: 血液循环把二氧化碳送回肺部。
senses.why: The stream image makes the blood a container of cargo, so one word can cover every substance in transit.
senses.whyCN: 河流意象把血液变成装载货物的容器，因此一个词就能涵盖一切在运输中的物质。

senses.title: A figurative mainstream
senses.titleCN: 比喻用法：进入主流或系统内部
senses.definition: figuratively, the main channel of a system, as when an idea enters the mainstream
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某个系统的主渠道，如某种观点进入主流
senses.example: The idea entered the bloodstream of the industry within a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这个想法一年之内进入了行业的主流。
senses.why: Once the stream is the body's main channel, any system's main channel can borrow the image.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这条河流成为身体的主渠道，任何系统的主渠道都能借用这个意象。

intro.en: Bloodstream is an English compound of blood, from Old English blod, and stream, from Old English stream. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: bloodstream 是英语复合词，由古英语 blod「血」与古英语 stream「水流」构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Blod is the native Germanic word for blood; its deeper Indo-European links are reconstructed rather than recorded.
items.cn: blod 是表示血的本族日耳曼词；其更深的印欧语联系属重构，并无记录。

items.en: Stream meant a flowing current of water. The metaphor of a bodily river was available as soon as the two words were joined.
items.cn: stream 指流动的水流。两个词一结合，身体里有一条河的比喻就自然成立。

items.en: The compound bloodstream is recorded in the nineteenth century, when physiology began describing the circulation as a single moving system. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: 复合词 bloodstream 记录于 19 世纪，当时生理学开始把循环描述成一个整体流动系统。最早的确切书证年代存疑。

items.en: Twentieth-century medicine fixed phrases such as bloodstream infection and levels in the bloodstream, treating the circulation as a measurable compartment.
items.cn: 20 世纪医学固定了 bloodstream infection、levels in the bloodstream 等短语，把循环视为可测量的隔室。

items.en: Journalism extended the word beyond the body, so that trends and ideas can enter the bloodstream of an organisation.
items.cn: 新闻写作把这个词扩展到身体之外，使潮流与观念也能进入某个组织的主流。

items.en: Source uncertainty: the exact first citation is uncertain, and the deeper origins of both blod and stream are reconstructions, not recorded forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代与更深词根）：最早书证年代存疑；blod 与 stream 的更深来源均属重构形式，而非有记录的实际词。

note.en: The first group holds the container-and-content words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for the circulation and its flow.
note.cn: 第一组是「容器与内容物」之间容易混淆的词；第二组是「循环及其流动」的近义词。

entries.definition: A tube that carries blood; bloodstream names what flows inside those tubes.
entries.definitionCN: 运送血液的管道；bloodstream 指管道里流动的东西。

entries.definition: The fluid tissue itself; bloodstream adds the idea of continuous circulation.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液这种流体组织本身；bloodstream 增加了持续循环的意思。

entries.definition: The movement of blood around the body; bloodstream can mean either the moving blood or the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 指血液在全身的运动；bloodstream 既可指流动的血液，也可指它构成的系统。

entries.definition: A specific diagnosis, not a synonym for the blood itself.
entries.definitionCN: 一个具体诊断，并不是血液本身的同义词。

entries.definition: The whole loop of heart, vessels and blood; it stresses the circuit rather than the fluid.
entries.definitionCN: 指心脏、血管与血液构成的整个环路，强调回路而非流体。

entries.definition: The movement of blood through a vessel or organ, often measured in volume per minute.
entries.definitionCN: 血液通过某条血管或某个器官的运动，常以每分钟体积计量。

entries.definition: The network of vessels itself; the bloodstream is what the network carries.
entries.definitionCN: 指血管网络本身；bloodstream 是该网络运送的内容。

entries.definition: The clear fluid left after blood clots; it is a laboratory fraction, not the circulating whole.
entries.definitionCN: 血液凝固后剩下的清液，是实验室组分，不是循环中的全血。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: blood + stream: blood pictured as a river running through the body.
normal.cn: blood + stream：把血液想象成流经全身的一条河。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: enter the bloodstream, bloodstream infection, in the bloodstream.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：进入血液、血流感染、在血液中。

normal.en: The family runs blood, bleed, bloody, blood-borne and bloodstream.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 blood、bleed、bloody、blood-borne、bloodstream。

normal.en: blood vessel is the container; bloodstream is the contents.
normal.cn: blood vessel 是容器，bloodstream 是内容物。

normal.en: The phrase usually takes 'the': the bloodstream.
normal.cn: 这个短语通常加 the：the bloodstream。

abstract.en: Picture a river network inside the body, with the heart as its pumping station.
abstract.cn: 想象体内一张河流网络，心脏是它的泵站。

abstract.en: Picture a pill dissolving and its molecules riding the current to every organ.
abstract.cn: 想象一片药溶解，分子随水流被带到每个器官。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour entering an organisation the way a solute enters the blood.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻进入某个组织，像溶质进入血液一样。

examples.en: Alcohol reaches the bloodstream within minutes of drinking.
examples.cn: 饮酒后几分钟内酒精就进入血液循环。

examples.en: The infection spread through the bloodstream to the joints.
examples.cn: 感染经血流扩散到关节。

examples.en: Doctors monitor drug levels in the bloodstream to avoid toxicity.
examples.cn: 医生监测血液中的药物浓度以避免毒性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「blood 血 + stream 河流」——血液像河一样在体内流动 → bloodstream 血液循环

root: 古英语 blod「血」+ 古英语 stream「水流」→ 英语复合词 bloodstream。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one current: blood is pictured as a river that supplies every tissue, carries drugs and germs, can be sampled, and can finally stand for the mainstream of any system.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一股水流展开：血液被想象成一条河，供应每个组织、运送药物与病菌、可被取样，最后也能代表任何系统的主流。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one continuous river of blood running through the whole body.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条贯穿全身、连续流动的血液之河。

branches.en: THE RIVER AND ITS CARGO: the circulating whole, the medium, and everything in transit.
branches.cn: 河流与货物：循环整体、介质，以及一切在运输中的东西。

branches.en: THE ARRIVAL AND THE READING: a substance enters, and then its level is measured.
branches.cn: 到达与读数：物质先进入，随后其水平被测量。

branches.en: THE HIGHWAY OF HARM: germs travel by blood, and bloodstream infection names the result.
branches.cn: 伤害的高速路：病菌经血传播，血流感染则命名其结果。

branches.en: THE CURRENT'S SPEED: the stream image also gives the word a rate.
branches.cn: 水流的速度：河流意象也赋予这个词一个速率。

branches.en: OUT OF THE BODY: the metaphor leaves anatomy and names the main channel of any system.
branches.cn: 离开身体：这个比喻脱离解剖，命名任何系统的主渠道。

intro.en: Bloodstream is a native compound of two Old English words, with no Latin suffix in its own structure.
intro.cn: bloodstream 是两个古英语词构成的本族复合词，自身结构中没有拉丁后缀。

latinIntro.en: The compound has no Latin source; its scientific relatives come from Latin vas 'vessel' and Greek haima 'blood', as in vascular and hematology.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词没有拉丁来源；它的科学同族词来自拉丁 vas「容器」与希腊 haima「血」，如 vascular 与 hematology。

items.example: The toxin entered the bloodstream quickly.
items.exampleCN: 毒素很快进入血液循环。

items.meaning: the red fluid of the body
items.example: Blood carries oxygen to the brain.
items.exampleCN: 血液把氧气送到大脑。

items.example: A stream ran beside the path.
items.exampleCN: 小径旁有一条溪流。

items.example: The wound bled for an hour.
items.exampleCN: 伤口流了一个小时的血。

items.example: He wiped his bloody hands.
items.exampleCN: 他擦掉了手上的血。

items.example: Hepatitis can be blood-borne.
items.exampleCN: 肝炎可经血液传播。

items.example: Vascular tissue distributes blood.
items.exampleCN: 血管组织分布血液。

items.example: Hematology covers anaemia and clotting.
items.exampleCN: 血液学涵盖贫血与凝血。

definition_en: a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart, or a main route in a transport or supply system
core_image: 一条从心脏出发、管壁厚而有弹性的血管，血液被压着向外流
scene: The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
sceneCN: 这里 artery 指「动脉」（第 1 个义项：把血液从心脏送出的血管）；句意：冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。图中可辨识物件：心脏、冠状动脉、分支血管、血流箭头。

pos.zh: 动脉（把血液从心脏送出的血管）；干线；命脉（比喻主要通道或供应线）

senses.title: Vessel away from the heart
senses.titleCN: 动脉：把血从心脏送出的血管
senses.definition: a thick-walled blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart
senses.definitionCN: 把血液从心脏送出的厚壁血管
senses.example: The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
senses.exampleCN: 冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。
senses.why: Greek arteria first named the windpipe; Galen later showed that these vessels carry blood, and the anatomical sense took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；盖伦后来证明这类管道运送血液，解剖义由此占据主导。

senses.title: A named artery
senses.titleCN: 具名动脉：主动脉、颈动脉、冠状动脉等
senses.definition: one of the large named vessels of the body, such as the aorta or carotid
senses.definitionCN: 体内有专名的大血管，如主动脉或颈动脉
senses.example: The carotid artery was narrowed by plaque.
senses.exampleCN: 颈动脉因斑块而变窄。
senses.why: Anatomy names individual arteries because each supplies a defined region.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学为各条动脉命名，因为每条供应一个确定区域。

senses.title: Oxygen-rich blood
senses.titleCN: 动脉血：含氧较高的血液
senses.definition: in ordinary usage, the oxygenated blood carried by most arteries
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中指大多数动脉所运的含氧血
senses.example: The artery carries bright red, oxygen-rich blood.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉运送鲜红、富氧的血液。
senses.why: Colour and oxygen came to stand for the vessel type, even though the pulmonary artery is the exception.
senses.whyCN: 颜色与含氧量被用来代表血管类型，尽管肺动脉是例外。

senses.title: Arterial disease
senses.titleCN: 动脉病变：硬化、狭窄与阻塞
senses.definition: a condition in which an artery thickens, narrows or blocks, restricting flow
senses.definitionCN: 动脉增厚、变窄或堵塞、限制血流的状况
senses.example: Peripheral artery disease makes walking painful.
senses.exampleCN: 外周动脉疾病使行走疼痛。
senses.why: Pathology attaches the vessel name to the condition, because the disease is defined by where it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 病理学把血管名称附着在病症上，因为这类疾病的定义就取决于它发生在哪里。

senses.title: A transport artery
senses.titleCN: 交通干线：城市或地区的主干道路
senses.definition: a main road or rail line that carries most of the traffic
senses.definitionCN: 承载大部分交通的主干道路或铁路线
senses.example: The new bridge became the city's main artery.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥成了这座城市的主干道。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the bodily image: a trunk route feeds the smaller routes as an artery feeds capillaries.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用身体意象：主干路线像动脉供养毛细血管一样供养小路。

senses.title: An economic lifeline
senses.titleCN: 经济命脉：关键的供应通道
senses.definition: a vital route or channel on which a region's economy depends
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区经济所依赖的关键路线或通道
senses.example: The strait is the artery of regional oil trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海峡是区域石油贸易的命脉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from roads to flows of goods, money or energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从道路扩展到货物、资金或能源的流动。

senses.title: A palpable pulse
senses.titleCN: 动脉搏动：可触摸到的跳动
senses.definition: the rhythmic beat felt where an artery lies near the skin
senses.definitionCN: 动脉靠近皮肤处可以摸到的节律性跳动
senses.example: The nurse felt the pulse in the radial artery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在桡动脉处摸到脉搏。
senses.why: An artery lying near the skin transmits its pressure wave, so the vessel name also names the felt beat.
senses.whyCN: 靠近皮肤的动脉会把压力波传出来，因此血管名称也用来命名可触摸到的跳动。

senses.title: The branching network
senses.titleCN: 动脉分支：越分越细的供血树
senses.definition: the branching tree of arteries that spreads from the heart to the tissues
senses.definitionCN: 从心脏向组织铺开、越分越细的动脉树
senses.example: Each artery divides until it becomes an arteriole.
senses.exampleCN: 每条动脉不断分支，直到变成小动脉。
senses.why: Anatomy describes arteries as a tree, since each trunk divides into ever finer branches.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把动脉描述成一棵树，因为每条主干都不断分成更细的枝。

senses.title: Artery as metaphor for strength
senses.titleCN: 命脉比喻：系统赖以生存的部分
senses.definition: figuratively, the part of a system without which it cannot function
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一个系统赖以运转、不可缺少的部分
senses.example: Young teachers are the artery of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻教师是这所学校的命脉。
senses.why: The image of a trunk feeding the whole body extends to any component a system cannot survive without.
senses.whyCN: 主干供养全身的意象，延伸到任何系统缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery comes from Latin arteria, from Greek arteria, which first named the windpipe. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: artery 出自拉丁 arteria，源于希腊 arteria，后者最初指气管。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek arteria named the windpipe and the air passages. The deeper origin of the word is disputed; one suggestion links ana- 'up' with terein 'to keep', but this is not established.
items.cn: 希腊 arteria 指气管与气道。这个词的更深来源有争议；一种说法把它与 ana-「向上」和 terein「守住」联系起来，但并未确立。

items.en: Galen's anatomical work distinguished arteries from veins and showed that arteries carry blood, not only air, fixing the medical sense.
items.cn: 盖伦的解剖工作把动脉与静脉区分开来，并证明动脉运送的是血而非只有气，从而固定了医学义。

items.en: Latin took arteria directly from Greek and used it for the blood vessels leading from the heart.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 arteria，用来指从心脏引出的血管。

items.en: English artery is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first in translations of medical texts.
items.cn: 英语 artery 记录于 14 世纪，最早见于医学文本的翻译。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward the word was applied to roads, rivers and trade routes that carry the main flow of a system.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，这个词被用于承载系统主流的道路、河流与贸易路线。

items.en: Source uncertainty (root and first date): the Greek etymology of arteria is disputed, and the first English citation is uncertain; any deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：arteria 的希腊语词源有争议，英语最早书证年代存疑；任何更深的印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds the vessel types and same-family words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for a main route or channel.
note.cn: 第一组是血管类型与同族易混词；第二组是「主要通道」的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to arteries, as in arterial blood; it describes, while artery names the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 与动脉有关，如动脉血；它描述性质，artery 则命名血管。

entries.definition: A small artery that leads into capillaries; it is narrower than an artery.
entries.definitionCN: 通向毛细血管的小动脉，比动脉细。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood back to the heart; the artery carries it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把血送回心脏的血管；动脉则把血送出去。

entries.definition: The main artery leaving the heart; it is one particular artery, not a synonym for all arteries.
entries.definitionCN: 离开心脏的主干动脉，是某一条具体动脉，不是所有动脉的同义词。

entries.definition: Any tube carrying blood, including arteries, veins and capillaries.
entries.definitionCN: 任何运血的管道，包括动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

entries.definition: A principal route of a railway or utility network; it matches the figurative sense of artery.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路或公用设施网络的主路线，对应 artery 的比喻义。

entries.definition: A route or link on which survival depends; it stresses necessity rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 生存所依赖的路线或联系，强调必要性而非规模。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or route between regions, often used for transport or wildlife.
entries.definitionCN: 地区之间的狭窄通道，常用于运输或野生动物迁徙。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek arteria first meant windpipe; anatomy later gave it to the blood vessel from the heart.
normal.cn: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；解剖学后来把它给了从心脏引出的血管。

normal.en: The family runs arterial, arteriole, arteritis, arteriosclerosis and endarterectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis、endarterectomy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: coronary artery, carotid artery, pulmonary artery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：冠状动脉、颈动脉、肺动脉。

normal.en: Arteries carry blood away; veins bring it back.
normal.cn: 动脉把血送出，静脉把血送回。

normal.en: A city's main road is called an artery because it feeds the smaller streets.
normal.cn: 城市主干道被称为 artery，因为它供养更小的街道。

abstract.en: Picture a thick elastic pipe leaving a pump and branching into thinner pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象一根有弹性的粗管离开泵，再分叉成更细的管子。

abstract.en: Picture a motorway feeding a whole city of small streets.
abstract.cn: 想象一条高速公路供养整座城市的小街道。
