abstract.en: Picture two fingers pressed on a wrist, counting a regular beat.
abstract.cn: 想象两根手指按在手腕上，数着规律的跳动。

examples.en: The surgeon cleared the blocked coronary artery with a stent.
examples.cn: 外科医生用支架打通了堵塞的冠状动脉。

examples.en: The river is the artery of trade for the whole valley.
examples.cn: 这条河是整个河谷的贸易命脉。

examples.en: Arteries thicken and stiffen with age.
examples.cn: 动脉会随年龄增长而增厚、变硬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arter 管道 + y」——从心脏向外送血的管道 → artery 动脉

root: 希腊 arteria「气管；动脉」→ 拉丁 arteria → 英语 artery。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one direction: blood is pushed away from the heart through a thick tube, and that tube becomes a named vessel, a diseased site, a main road, an economic lifeline, a pulse, a branching tree and finally a metaphor for a system's vital part.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个方向展开：血液被从心脏压进一根厚管，而这根管子依次成为具名血管、病变部位、主干道路、经济命脉、可触脉搏、分叉树，最后成为系统命脉的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick elastic tube carrying blood outward from the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根厚而有弹性的管子，把血液从心脏向外送出。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND THE TREE: one artery, its proper name, and the branching network it starts.
branches.cn: 管子与树：一条动脉、它的专名，以及它开启的分叉网络。

branches.en: THE OXYGEN COLOUR: bright red blood came to stand for the vessel type.
branches.cn: 含氧的颜色：鲜红的血被用来代表这类血管。

branches.en: THE BODY'S SIGNALS: disease can be seen in the wall, and health can be felt as a pulse.
branches.cn: 身体的信号：病变可见于管壁，健康可感于脉搏。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR OF ROUTES: roads and trade channels feed a region as arteries feed tissue.
branches.cn: 路线比喻：道路与贸易通道供养一个地区，正如动脉供养组织。

branches.en: THE VITAL PART: any system has a component it cannot live without.
branches.cn: 命脉部分：任何系统都有一个缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery is a Greek noun taken into Latin with little change; its English derivatives are built on the stem arteri-.
intro.cn: artery 是几乎原样进入拉丁语的希腊名词；其英语派生词都建在词干 arteri- 上。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin arteria supply arterial, arteriole, arteritis and arteriosclerosis; the Greek origin is shared, and the deeper root is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语 arteria 提供 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis；其希腊来源是共有的，更深词根有争议。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The artery was cleared with a stent.
items.exampleCN: 这条动脉用支架打通了。

items.example: Arterial blood is bright red.
items.exampleCN: 动脉血是鲜红色的。

items.example: Arterioles control blood pressure.
items.exampleCN: 小动脉控制血压。

items.example: Giant cell arteritis affects the scalp vessels.
items.exampleCN: 巨细胞动脉炎影响头皮血管。

items.example: Arteriosclerosis develops slowly over decades.
items.exampleCN: 动脉硬化在数十年间缓慢发展。

items.meaning: surgical removal of plaque from inside an artery
items.meaningCN: 从动脉内壁切除斑块的手术
items.example: Carotid endarterectomy lowers stroke risk.
items.exampleCN: 颈动脉内膜切除术降低中风风险。

items.meaning: a main road in a transport network
items.meaningCN: 交通网络中的主干道路
items.example: The arterial road carries traffic around the city.
items.exampleCN: 这条主干道承载绕城交通。

items.meaning: the main artery from the heart
items.example: The aorta is the body's largest artery.
items.exampleCN: 主动脉是体内最大的动脉。

definition_zh: 动脉的；动脉血的；主干道路的
definition_en: relating to an artery or to blood carried by arteries, or describing a main route in a transport network
core_image: 一条厚壁动脉里鲜红的血被压着流向组织
scene: The ambulance raced along the arterial road to the hospital.
sceneCN: 这里 arterial 指「主干道路的」（第 7 个义项：城市交通网络中的主要通道）；句意：救护车沿主干道疾驰前往医院。图中可辨识物件：宽阔道路、救护车、路牌、城市街区。

pos.zh: 动脉的；动脉血的；主干道路的（交通用语）

senses.title: Relating to an artery
senses.titleCN: 动脉的：与动脉这一结构有关
senses.definition: connected with an artery as an anatomical structure
senses.definitionCN: 与作为解剖结构的动脉有关
senses.example: Arterial walls are thicker than venous walls.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉壁比静脉壁厚。
senses.why: Latin -alis forms a relational adjective, so arterial begins as 'of an artery'.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 -alis 构成关系形容词，因此 arterial 起初意为「属于动脉的」。

senses.title: Arterial blood
senses.titleCN: 动脉血的：含氧丰富的血
senses.definition: describes oxygenated blood such as that in most arteries
senses.definitionCN: 形容含氧丰富的血液，如大多数动脉中的血
senses.example: Arterial blood is bright red because haemoglobin is saturated.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉血因血红蛋白饱和而呈鲜红色。
senses.why: The adjective moved from the vessel to its usual contents, so 'arterial' can describe blood composition.
senses.whyCN: 形容词从血管转到其常见内容物，因此 arterial 可以描述血液成分。

senses.title: Arterial pressure
senses.titleCN: 动脉压：动脉内的血压
senses.definition: the pressure of blood inside the arteries, usually reported as systolic and diastolic values
senses.definitionCN: 动脉内的血液压力，通常以收缩压与舒张压报告
senses.example: Arterial pressure falls sharply in severe bleeding.
senses.exampleCN: 严重出血时动脉压急剧下降。
senses.why: Pressure is measured inside the artery, so the adjective marks both the site and the quantity.
senses.whyCN: 压力是在动脉内部测得的，因此这个形容词既标出位置，也标出所测的量。

senses.title: Arterial disease
senses.titleCN: 动脉疾病的：硬化、狭窄与炎症
senses.definition: describes conditions that affect arteries, such as atherosclerosis
senses.definitionCN: 形容影响动脉的病症，如动脉粥样硬化
senses.example: Arterial disease in the legs limits walking distance.
senses.exampleCN: 腿部动脉疾病会限制行走距离。
senses.why: The adjective names the affected structures rather than the illness, a common pattern in clinical labels.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词命名的是受影响的组织结构，而非疾病本身，这是临床标签中的常见模式。

senses.title: Arterial supply
senses.titleCN: 动脉供血的：某个器官的动脉来源
senses.definition: describes the arteries that supply a particular organ or region
senses.definitionCN: 形容供应某个器官或区域的动脉
senses.example: The brain's arterial supply comes mainly from the carotids.
senses.exampleCN: 大脑的动脉供血主要来自颈动脉。
senses.why: Anatomy speaks of the arterial supply because the arteries are the source of blood to a region.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学说「动脉供血」，因为动脉是某个区域血液的来源。

senses.title: Arterial route of delivery
senses.titleCN: 经动脉途径：药物或器械进入动脉
senses.definition: describes access through an artery, as in arterial injection or arterial line
senses.definitionCN: 形容经动脉进入的方式，如动脉注射或动脉置管
senses.example: Contrast was injected by the arterial route.
senses.exampleCN: 造影剂经动脉途径注入。
senses.why: Procedures name the access route, and entering through an artery is described by the same adjective.
senses.whyCN: 操作要命名进入的路径，而经动脉进入正是用同一个形容词来描述。

senses.title: Arterial road
senses.titleCN: 主干道路：承担主要交通的通道
senses.definition: in transport, a main road that carries traffic between districts
senses.definitionCN: 交通中指承担各区之间车流的主要道路
senses.example: The ambulance raced along the arterial road to the hospital.
senses.exampleCN: 救护车沿主干道疾驰前往医院。
senses.why: The bodily image of a trunk feeding branches was transferred to road networks in the twentieth century.
senses.whyCN: 20 世纪，把主干供养分支的身体意象转移到道路网络。

senses.title: Arterial bleeding
senses.titleCN: 动脉出血：喷射状的快速失血
senses.definition: describes bleeding from a cut artery, which spurts with each heartbeat
senses.definitionCN: 形容动脉被割破后的出血，随心跳喷射
senses.example: Arterial bleeding must be controlled at once.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉出血必须立即止血。
senses.why: The spurting character of the bleeding comes from arterial pressure, so the adjective marks both source and appearance.
senses.whyCN: 出血呈喷射状源于动脉压力，因此这个形容词既标出来源，也标出表现。

intro.en: Arterial is the Latin relational adjective arterialis, built on arteria. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: arterial 是拉丁关系形容词 arterialis，由 arteria 构成。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek arteria first named the windpipe; its deeper origin is disputed, and no single etymology is accepted.
items.cn: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；其更深来源有争议，没有公认的单一词源。

items.en: Latin borrowed arteria and, after Galen, used it chiefly for the vessels carrying blood from the heart.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 arteria，并在盖伦之后主要用它指从心脏运血的血管。

items.en: Arterialis was formed with -alis 'relating to'. It appears in later medical Latin rather than in classical prose.
items.cn: arterialis 由 -alis「与……有关」构成，见于后世医学拉丁，而非古典散文。

items.en: English arterial enters in the sixteenth century, first in medical descriptions and later in general writing about main routes.
items.cn: 英语 arterial 于 16 世纪进入，最早见于医学描述，后来也用于关于主干路线的普通写作。

items.en: Twentieth-century planning adopted 'arterial road' for the main roads of a city, extending the anatomical metaphor.
items.cn: 20 世纪城市规划采用 arterial road 指城市主干道，延伸了解剖学比喻。

items.en: Source uncertainty (root and first date): the Greek etymology of arteria is disputed, and the first English citation is uncertain; any deeper form is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：arteria 的希腊词源有争议，英语最早书证年代存疑；任何更深形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds words of the same family and the opposite vessel type; the second holds near-synonyms for a main route and for blood-related adjectives.
note.cn: 第一组是同族词与相反血管类型；第二组是「主要通道」及「血液相关形容词」的近义词。

entries.definition: The vessel itself; arterial is the adjective describing it or its contents.
entries.definitionCN: 指血管本身；arterial 是描述它或其内容物的形容词。

entries.definition: A small artery leading to capillaries; it is a noun, not an adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 通向毛细血管的小动脉，是名词，不是形容词。

entries.definition: Relating to veins and to blood returning to the heart; it is the counterpart of arterial.
entries.definitionCN: 与静脉及回流心脏的血有关，是 arterial 的对应词。

entries.definition: Inflammation of an artery; it names a condition, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 动脉的炎症，命名一种病症而非属性。

entries.definition: Relating to vessels of any kind, arterial or venous; it is broader than arterial.
entries.definitionCN: 与任何血管有关，包括动脉与静脉，比 arterial 范围广。

entries.definition: Relating to the arteries that supply the heart muscle; narrower than arterial.
entries.definitionCN: 指供应心肌的动脉，比 arterial 范围窄。

entries.definition: The everyday term for an arterial road; it lacks the metaphor of the trunk feeding branches.
entries.definitionCN: 主干道路的日常说法，没有「主干供养分支」的比喻。

entries.definition: A major road connecting cities; like arterial road, it borrows a body metaphor.
entries.definitionCN: 连接城市的主要道路，与 arterial road 一样借用身体比喻。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: artery + -al 'relating to': the adjective of the artery.
normal.cn: artery + -al「与……有关」：动脉的形容词。

normal.en: The family runs artery, arteriole, arteritis, arteriosclerosis and arterialize.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 artery、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis、arterialize。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the clinic: arterial blood, arterial pressure, arterial blood gas, arterial disease.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出临床语境：动脉血、动脉压、动脉血气、动脉疾病。

normal.en: venous is the opposite of arterial.
normal.cn: venous 是 arterial 的反向对应词。

normal.en: An arterial road is a city's main road, borrowed from the body.
normal.cn: arterial road 是城市主干道，借自身体意象。

abstract.en: Picture thick-walled pipes carrying bright red blood under pressure.
abstract.cn: 想象厚壁管道在压力下运送鲜红的血。

abstract.en: Picture a wide road with ambulances and buses moving fast between districts.
abstract.cn: 想象一条宽阔道路，救护车与公交在城区之间快速穿行。

abstract.en: Picture a sample tube of arterial blood, bright red against a dark background.
abstract.cn: 想象一支动脉血样管，在深色背景下呈鲜红。

examples.en: Arterial blood gas results showed low oxygen.
examples.cn: 动脉血气结果显示出低氧。

examples.en: Arterial stiffness rises with age and high blood pressure.
examples.cn: 动脉僵硬度随年龄与高血压上升。

examples.en: The city plans to widen its main arterial roads.
examples.cn: 这座城市计划拓宽主要干道。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「artery 动脉 + al 的」——与动脉有关的 → arterial 动脉的

root: 希腊 arteria「气管；动脉」→ 拉丁 arteria → 拉丁形容词 arterialis → 英语 arterial。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one tube: the adjective of an artery can describe its wall, its blood, its pressure, its diseases, its supply, its use as a route, and finally a city's main road.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一根管子展开：动脉的形容词可描述管壁、其中的血、压力、疾病、供血、作为通道的用途，最后还可描述城市主干道。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick-walled tube carrying bright red blood outward under pressure.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根厚壁管在压力下把鲜红的血向外送出。

branches.en: TUBE AND CONTENTS: the adjective describes the wall and the oxygen-rich blood inside it.
branches.cn: 管子与内容：这个形容词既描述管壁，也描述其中的富氧血。

branches.en: MEASURE AND FAILURE: pressure is the number, disease is the breakdown.
branches.cn: 测量与故障：压力是数字，疾病是崩溃。

branches.en: SUPPLY AND ACCESS: the arteries that feed an organ also provide a route for drugs and lines.
branches.cn: 供应与通道：供养器官的动脉同时也提供给药与置管的路径。

branches.en: THE SIGN OF DAMAGE: arterial bleeding spurts because the blood is under pressure.
branches.cn: 损伤信号：动脉出血呈喷射状，因为血处于压力之下。

branches.en: OUT OF THE BODY: the same adjective names a main road feeding smaller streets.
branches.cn: 离开身体：同一形容词命名供养小街道的主干道。

intro.en: Arterial is a Greek-derived noun stem plus the Latin relational suffix -alis: arteri- + -al.
intro.cn: arterial 是希腊来源名词词干加拉丁关系后缀 -alis：arteri- + -al。

latinIntro.en: Latin arteria gives artery, arterial, arteriole, arteritis and arteriosclerosis; the Greek source is shared, though its deeper etymology is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 arteria 给出 artery、arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis；其希腊来源为共有，但更深词源有争议。

items.example: Arterial walls contain smooth muscle.
items.exampleCN: 动脉壁含有平滑肌。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The artery was blocked by plaque.
items.exampleCN: 这条动脉被斑块堵塞。

items.example: Arterioles regulate local flow.
items.exampleCN: 小动脉调节局部血流。

items.example: Arteritis can cause headaches and blindness.
items.exampleCN: 动脉炎可导致头痛与失明。

items.example: Arteriosclerosis narrows the lumen.
items.exampleCN: 动脉硬化使管腔变窄。

items.meaning: to make arterial, as blood in the lungs
items.example: The lungs arterialize venous blood.
items.exampleCN: 肺使静脉血动脉化。

items.meaning: a test of oxygen and carbon dioxide in arterial blood
items.meaningCN: 检测动脉血中氧气与二氧化碳的检查
items.example: Arterial blood gas guides ventilator settings.
items.exampleCN: 动脉血气指导呼吸机参数。

items.meaning: a main road carrying traffic between districts
items.meaningCN: 承担城区间车流的主要道路
items.example: Buses use the arterial road every ten minutes.
items.exampleCN: 公交每十分钟沿主干道运行一次。
